source_quote: Headspace was great when it had a meaningful free tier. Now you can barely try it before hitting the paywall

title: Subscription cost itself causes anxiety
problem: Paying high yearly fees for an anxiety app feels wrong and creates money worry, undermining the point of using it.
workaround: cancel and rely on free breathing exercises
source_quote: the subscription prices give them anxiety

title: Sunday-evening dread with no outlet
problem: Anxiety about the coming work week ruins Sunday nights every week and there is no structured way to defuse it.
workaround: distraction, alcohol

title: Therapy homework forgotten between sessions
problem: Worksheets and exercises assigned in therapy are lost or forgotten, so each session restarts the same conversation.
workaround: paper handouts, phone notes

title: Too much content to choose from
problem: Hundreds of meditations and sleep stories make the app menu overwhelming, so a stressed person gives up before picking one.
who: stressed users of large wellness apps
workaround: replay the same one session
source_quote: Calm's menus can feel a bit crowded sometimes due to the massive amount of content available

title: Calendar silently allows double booking
problem: Accepting an invite that overlaps an existing event produces no warning, and the clash is only discovered when both meetings start.
workaround: eyeball the day view before accepting
source_quote: Calendar doesn't alert double-booking event conflict

title: Email ping-pong to find a meeting slot
problem: Agreeing a time with two or more people takes days of proposing, declining and re-proposing before anything lands on a calendar.
who: professionals, freelancers, anyone organizing a group
workaround: booking links, polls, or one person dictating
source_quote: the most laborious part of the meeting-planning process is the back and forth

title: Event and its notification in different time zones
problem: After travel or a device settings change, the calendar shows one time while the alert fires at another, so reminders arrive hours off.
workaround: manually re-check every event after landing
source_quote: Calendar and notifications are on two different time zones.

title: Work and personal calendars clash unseen
problem: A dentist appointment in the personal calendar is invisible to the work booking page, so colleagues book meetings on top of it.
who: people with separate work and personal accounts
workaround: manually copy busy blocks between calendars
source_quote: the double-booking problem continues even with Google Calendar

title: Your time or my time confusion
problem: Proposing a meeting time across zones triggers a chain of clarifying emails, and a wrong guess means someone shows up an hour early or misses it.
who: remote and distributed teams, freelancers with overseas clients
workaround: world clock sites, writing times in both zones
source_quote: the email ping-pong of "Wait, did you mean 3pm YOUR time or MY time?"

title: Booking page shows wrong time zone
problem: A public booking form displays slots in UTC or the host's zone, so guests book the wrong hour or abandon the form.
who: consultants, coaches, anyone sharing a booking link
workaround: add a note asking guests to convert times
source_quote: the time zone is wrong, showing up in the booking form as UTC

title: Daylight-saving shifts break cross-zone plans
problem: Recurring calls with people abroad silently move by an hour for a few weeks each spring and autumn, and someone always misses one.
workaround: remembering to warn everyone in advance

title: Same people always get the 7am call
problem: Across a distributed team the inconvenient early or late slots keep landing on the same colleagues because nobody tracks the fairness of meeting times.
who: distributed teams spanning many time zones
workaround: none
source_quote: colleagues who always seem to be the ones dialing in at 7 a.m. or 9 p.m.

title: Capturing a thought while hands are busy
problem: A task comes to mind while driving, cooking or in the shower and there is no frictionless way to catch it before it evaporates.
workaround: voice assistant, texting yourself

title: Forgetting essentials on the way out
problem: Keys, wallet, badge, lunch or the parcel to return get left behind because there is no checkpoint at the door.
workaround: bowl by the door, mental checklist
source_quote: refresh your memory before you head out

title: Forgetting short background timers
problem: Laundry in the washer, the oven, the parking meter and the kettle are forgotten because starting them and remembering them are separate acts.
who: everyone at home, drivers using metered parking
workaround: voice-assistant timers, alarms

title: Infrequent chores never come back
problem: Every-few-months jobs like replacing a filter, flipping the mattress, renewing a passport or a car inspection are forgotten because nothing repeats that slowly in the head.
workaround: none, or stickers with dates

title: Remembering to bring the right things
problem: Gym kit on Tuesday, library books on Thursday, the form for the school trip: what to pack depends on the day's events and gets forgotten.
workaround: packing the night before, sticky notes

title: Sticky notes become invisible
problem: Visual reminders left in plain sight stop registering within days, so the note on the door no longer prevents forgetting.
who: people who use physical or on-screen visual cues
workaround: move the note somewhere new
source_quote: the visual reminder becomes visual noise, which you can stop seeing even after a short while

title: Waiting-for items fall through the cracks
problem: Things other people owe you (a reply, a refund, a document) are not tasks you can do, so they live nowhere and are only remembered weeks later.
who: anyone who delegates or deals with services
workaround: starred emails, a 'waiting' tag

title: Scary task grows scarier each day
problem: A big, vague, urgent item sits ignored on the list and every day it stays there it becomes harder to even look at.
workaround: none, or panic near the deadline
source_quote: the longer they sit, the bigger and scarier they become

title: Planning eats the time for doing
problem: Rewriting, re-sorting and re-tooling the to-do list becomes the activity, and the tasks themselves are never started.
workaround: none
source_quote: spending all my time on making to do lists

title: Snoozing a task until it is forgotten
problem: Hitting 'remind me later' repeatedly pushes an item past its usefulness, and the app never escalates or flags how many times it has been deferred.
workaround: none

title: System breaks when life changes
problem: A routine that worked during term time or one job collapses after a schedule change, and rebuilding it from scratch is so costly people give up.
who: students, new parents, shift workers, job changers
workaround: abandon the system for weeks
source_quote: the system that worked in one phase of life can become useless when an entire schedule changes

title: Dismissed reminder is gone for good
problem: One accidental swipe clears a reminder and it never returns, so the thing it protected is forgotten until it is too late.
workaround: nagging-style apps that repeat every minute
source_quote: it'll annoy you every minute until you deal with the reminder

title: Quiet ping missed while in deep focus
problem: A single soft notification is not noticed when the user is absorbed, stressed or overstimulated, and there is no second chance.
workaround: loud alarms for everything, which then get disabled
source_quote: a soft ping on your phone is too quiet and too easy to miss

title: Reminder fires too late to act
problem: An alert 15 minutes before an appointment across town arrives after the moment one needed to leave, so it announces lateness rather than preventing it.
who: people with ADHD and anyone with in-person appointments
workaround: set multiple manual alerts for each event
source_quote: A notification at 9:15 for a 9:30 appointment isn't a reminder—it's an announcement.

title: Reminders decay into ignorable noise
problem: Every notification demands a micro-decision, and after enough of them the user swipes them all away without reading, including the important ones.
who: people who rely on phone notifications
workaround: turn everything off, or nothing off
source_quote: every time a notification pops up, it presents a micro-decision

title: Default reminder lead time is wrong
problem: Every event alerts a fixed 10 or 30 minutes ahead regardless of whether it is a call at the desk or a trip across town, so alerts are ignored or too late.
who: calendar users with mixed in-person and remote events
workaround: edit the reminder on each event by hand
source_quote: increased the default reminder time in Google Calendar to one hour instead of the default 30 minutes

title: Reminder tied to a person, not a time
problem: 'Ask Mom about the recipe' has no time attached; it needs to surface the next time you call or see her, which no time-based reminder can do.
workaround: notes app list per person

title: Morning routine loses track of time
problem: Between phone scrolling, the shower and breakfast there is no sense of how far behind the morning is until it is already too late to be on time.
who: people who are always late in the morning, ADHD adults
workaround: multiple alarms

title: No travel buffer between appointments
problem: Two in-person events get booked adjacent on the calendar even though it takes 25 minutes to get between them.
who: field workers, parents, people with errands
workaround: manually block 'travel' events

title: Getting-ready time not counted
problem: Leave-by alerts count only the drive, not the shower, dressing and finding keys, so people are still reliably 15 minutes late.
who: people who are always late in the morning
workaround: set the alarm earlier and still run late

title: Leave-by alerts ignore transit and bikes
problem: Departure reminders assume driving or walking, so people who take buses, trains or bikes get leave times that are simply wrong.
workaround: check the transit app separately and guess
source_quote: only offers options for driving or walking and doesn't provide time estimations for public transportation or biking

title: Meeting overruns cascade into lateness
problem: One meeting running ten minutes over makes the next one late, and the whole afternoon slides with no automatic warning to the later attendees.
workaround: manually message 'running 5 late'

title: Missed pickups when term schedules change
problem: Each new school term brings new activity times and locations, and the old calendar entries linger until a missed pickup exposes the gap.
workaround: re-enter everything by hand each September
source_quote: usually in September after a missed pickup

title: Family calendar goes stale
problem: Entering activities becomes one parent's chore, the chore lapses, the calendar stops matching reality and everyone stops trusting it.
workaround: paper calendar on the fridge, group chat
source_quote: entry became someone's chore and the chore stopped happening — so the calendar went stale

title: Shared events only remind the creator
problem: A shared family event alerts the person who entered it, but not the partner or teen who actually needs to show up.
workaround: text everyone the morning of
source_quote: shared family calendar that sends reminder prompts to everyone?

title: Shared reminders across iPhone and Android
problem: Mixed-platform households cannot share a single reminder or list that pings both phones, so each system only covers half the family.
who: couples and families with different phone platforms
workaround: messaging apps, duplicate entries

title: Verbal plans never reach the calendar
problem: 'Let's grab lunch Thursday' agreed in conversation is never written down, and one side forgets or double-books.
workaround: text to confirm the day before

title: Chronically underestimating task duration
problem: Tasks are planned to take 30 minutes and take two hours, so every daily plan collapses by noon and nothing is learned from the miss.
who: nearly everyone who plans a day
workaround: double all estimates
source_quote: difficulty estimating task length (10%)

title: Due dates without start times
problem: A task with a deadline gives no cue about when work must begin, so multi-hour tasks are started an hour before they are due.
who: students, people with ADHD, deadline-driven workers
workaround: manually create a separate 'start X' task
source_quote: shows you when to START tasks — not just when they're due

title: Interruptions derail the planned day
problem: Colleagues, messages and calls break the schedule repeatedly and there is no easy way to re-slot what was displaced.
workaround: do-not-disturb modes, working late
source_quote: Too many interruptions (40%)

title: Suddenly it is 8 PM
problem: Hours vanish into one activity and the user only notices when the day is gone and planned tasks were never touched.
who: people with time blindness, hyperfocus, remote workers
workaround: hourly chimes, visual timers
source_quote: prevent the "Wait, it's already 8 PM?!" experience

title: No idea where the day went
problem: At the end of a busy day it is impossible to say what the hours were spent on, so the same leaks repeat tomorrow.
workaround: manual time tracking that is abandoned within a week

title: Wasting the 20-minute gap
problem: A short unexpected gap between meetings is lost to scrolling because it is not obvious which small task fits it.
workaround: none

title: Day starts with 100 overdue tasks
problem: Rescheduled and overdue tasks pile into today, so each morning opens with a wall of red that is exhausting rather than useful.
workaround: scripts that auto-reschedule, or bulk-postponing everything
source_quote: having a large list of tasks creates 'cognitive drag' and stresses users out

title: Easy tasks crowd out important ones
problem: With no visible priority the user ticks off small quick wins all day while the thing that matters stays untouched.
who: anyone working from a flat list
workaround: eat-the-frog rules, stars and flags
source_quote: people tend to take the easiest task off the list rather than focusing on what's important

title: Overlong list, no idea what to start
problem: Dozens of open tasks stare back and the user freezes, unsure which one to actually work on right now.
who: anyone who captures everything into one list
workaround: pick three on paper each morning
source_quote: putting too many tasks on a to-do list can cause users to feel overwhelmed and unsure which task to work on

title: Tasks buried in chat and email
problem: Requests arrive in Slack threads, texts and emails and never make it into the task list, so they are lost once the message scrolls away.
workaround: flagging messages, 'mark unread'

title: Guilt from constantly rescheduling tasks
problem: Pushing the same task from day to day feels like failure, and the growing pile of postponements discourages opening the app at all.
who: people with more tasks than time
workaround: delete the task, or ignore the overdue count
source_quote: you should feel zero guilt for btw, it happens to the best of us

title: No usable log of what was completed
problem: Once a task is checked off it disappears, so at review time or when writing a status report there is no record of what actually got done last week.
who: knowledge workers who report on their work
workaround: keep a separate done-list or search email history
source_quote: todo apps lack a record of completed work that can be referred to for reports

title: One slip breaks the dependent chain
problem: When a task slips, the tasks that depend on it keep their old dates, so the plan is instantly wrong and must be rebuilt by hand.
workaround: drag every date manually

title: Recurring task misfires when done out of order
problem: Completing a recurring task early or late does not move it to the correct next occurrence, so the list shows it due again at the wrong time.
who: anyone using a to-do app for chores and routines
workaround: manually edit the due date after each completion
source_quote: apps failing to skip to the next recurring date when tasks are completed out of order

title: Tasks out of sync between phone and laptop
problem: A task ticked off on the phone still shows as open on the laptop, or an edit is lost, so people stop trusting the list.
who: people who use a to-do app on more than one device
workaround: force-refresh, or keep the list on one device only
source_quote: Sync issues across platforms plague many apps since their beginning.

title: Complex repeat patterns need duplicate tasks
problem: A task that repeats Monday, Wednesday and Friday, or on the first weekday of the month, cannot be expressed, forcing several redundant copies.
who: people with irregular routines (medication, classes, shifts)
workaround: create three separate recurring tasks
source_quote: doesn't have a very robust recurring task management system (e.g., MWF in a single week)

title: Tasks rot in the list for years
problem: Someday-maybe items sit in the list indefinitely, never surfaced or retired, cluttering every view and making the list feel dead.
workaround: periodic purge, or start a fresh app
source_quote: tasks that have lingered in pending status for years

title: Car in the shop, commute broken
problem: When the car is unavailable for a few days people scramble to piece together transit, rides and borrowed cars for each day.
workaround: ask family, expensive ride-hails

title: Carpool logistics buried in text threads
problem: Once a carpool exists, who is driving, who is sick, and who owes gas money is tracked in a messy group chat that people miss.
workaround: group text, mental accounting
source_quote: they manage them through informal channels like text rather than apps

title: Carpool match takes too long
problem: Commuters try a carpool app, cannot find a match on their route and schedule within a few days, and abandon it.
workaround: ask coworkers directly, drive alone
source_quote: if they can't find a match quickly, they leave the platform because it offers no added value

title: Combining modes into one trip
problem: A commute that mixes driving, a train and a bike share means juggling three apps, three payments and no single ETA.
workaround: several apps open at once
source_quote: integrated multimodal platforms... commuters' demand for seamless integration

title: Hybrid days and commute planning
problem: Office days shift week to week, so carpool partners, parking permits and transit passes are never aligned with the days someone actually goes in.
workaround: calendar juggling, over-buying passes

title: Bike lane blocked by snow or debris
problem: Snow, glass and construction shrink or close bike lanes with no warning, pushing riders into car traffic mid-route.
workaround: scout the route, ask local cycling groups
source_quote: Snow on road sides reducing space for bikes increases conflicts with cars

title: Nowhere secure to park the bike
problem: Riders do not know before arriving whether the office or destination has secure bike parking or a shower, so they risk theft or skip riding.
who: bike commuters to offices and appointments
workaround: ask reception, lock to a signpost
source_quote: Needing secure bike storage and facilities to clean up after riding

title: Bike commute takes far longer
problem: New bike commuters underestimate how much longer riding takes than driving, arrive late, and cannot predict the time for a given route and fitness level.
workaround: trial rides on the weekend, add a buffer
source_quote: Commute time is significantly longer than driving, requiring significant time adjustments

title: Bike lights dead when leaving
problem: Rechargeable bike lights are flat exactly when it gets dark early, and riders find out at the bike rack after work.
who: bike commuters in fall and winter
workaround: spare lights, charge at desk

title: Bike rack on bus already full
problem: Cyclists reach the bus stop with a bike and the two-slot front rack is taken, so they wait for the next bus or ride the whole way.
workaround: leave earlier, ride the full distance

title: Rain decision before leaving
problem: Cyclists must decide by 7am whether the ride home at 6pm will be wet and dangerous, and general weather apps do not answer that question for a route.
workaround: check hourly forecast, keep transit fare as backup
source_quote: Riding in rain is uncomfortable and hazardous in traffic

title: Tires and tubes wear out unnoticed
problem: City debris chews through tires and tubes, and riders only find out via a flat on the way to work because nothing tracks wear or mileage.
workaround: carry a spare tube, inspect by eye
source_quote: Bike tires and tubes wear quickly due to city street debris

title: Winter layering eats commute time
problem: Picking the right layers for the temperature and wind takes trial and error each morning and adds ten minutes to getting out the door.
workaround: notes on what worked last time
source_quote: Managing layers in winter is annoying and can add 10 minutes to commute time

title: Bad commute ruins the day
problem: An unexpectedly bad drive in leaves people stressed, late and rattled, and they had no warning that today was going to be worse than usual.
workaround: check traffic before leaving, leave early every day
source_quote: 68 percent of Americans said their whole day could be ruined by a bad commute

title: Chained school drop-off commute
problem: Dropping kids at school then getting to work involves fixed windows and pickup lines, and navigation apps do not plan around the timed stop.
workaround: leave extra early, mental scheduling

title: Everyone gets the same detour
problem: When traffic hits, the navigation app sends every driver down the same side street, so the detour becomes as jammed as the original route within minutes.
who: drivers who rely on Waze or Google Maps
workaround: ignore the reroute, use local knowledge
source_quote: when everyone receives the same detour, the detour becomes as mobbed as the regular route

title: Not knowing when to leave
problem: Commute time swings by 20-40 minutes day to day, and drivers have no reliable way to know the right departure minute for their specific route and arrival time.
workaround: leave early, check maps repeatedly while getting ready
source_quote: Traffic Congestion Down, Pain Way Up

title: Saved trips vanish from nav app
problem: Planned or saved commute routes disappear from the navigation app and the app lags or crashes mid-drive, forcing drivers to re-enter destinations at the wheel.
workaround: re-enter the address, switch apps
source_quote: the app crashing, traffic support missing, planned trips disappearing, a lag that makes the app hard to use

title: Surprise toll bills by mail
problem: Cashless toll roads, rental cars and out-of-state trips produce toll invoices weeks later with admin fees, and drivers cannot tell which trips they were for.
workaround: keep a transponder, log trips manually

title: Cheapest gas on the actual route
problem: Gas price apps show stations nearby, not which one is on the way home with the smallest detour, so drivers overpay or waste time.
workaround: GasBuddy plus mental math

title: Public charger broken on arrival
problem: EV commuters drive to a charger and find it dead, throwing an error, or stuck on a payment screen, with no way to know beforehand.
who: EV drivers relying on public charging
workaround: check recent check-ins on PlugShare, keep a fallback
source_quote: 72% said they had encountered a non-working charger

title: Charging spots occupied or ICE'd
problem: All chargers are taken, often by gas cars or fully charged EVs that never left, and there is no real-time availability or turn-taking.
who: EV commuters charging at work or lots
workaround: leave a note, come back later
source_quote: parking lots with gas-powered vehicles in EV charging spots, with all spots consistently filled

title: Too many charging payment apps
problem: Each charging network needs its own account, card or app, so drivers juggle half a dozen logins and fail to start a session.
workaround: install every network app, carry RFID cards
source_quote: too many ways to pay and users still using multiple payment methods

title: Commuter benefit receipts and claims
problem: Pre-tax transit or parking benefits require collecting receipts and filing claims each month, and unused balances quietly expire.
workaround: shoebox of receipts, forgetting

title: Logging mileage for reimbursement
problem: Employees who drive between sites reconstruct trips at month end from memory for mileage claims, and lose money on trips they forgot.
workaround: notebook in the car, guessing

title: Multiple agencies, multiple fare apps
problem: A trip crossing a bus agency, a regional rail line and a ferry means separate tickets and apps, with no single pass or fare cap.
workaround: several fare apps, physical cards

title: Monthly pass or pay per ride?
problem: With variable office days riders cannot tell whether a monthly pass or per-trip fare is cheaper, and they find out only after the money is spent.
workaround: guess, spreadsheet

title: Tracking true cost of the commute
problem: Drivers have no idea what their commute really costs in fuel, tolls, parking and wear, so they cannot compare it with transit or moving closer.
workaround: rough estimate once a year

title: Paid in app, ticketed anyway

problem: Street-sweeping and alternate-side rules change with holidays and suspensions, so residents either move the car needlessly or wake up to a ticket.
who: on-street parkers in cities with sweeping rules

problem: The commuter lot fills by 7:30 and drivers only find out on arrival, then miss the train hunting for street parking.
who: suburban rail commuters who drive to the station

source_quote: zone and lot confusion in dense urban areas

problem: In large garages or unfamiliar streets people forget the level, row or block where they left the car and wander for ten minutes.
who: drivers using large lots and garages
workaround: photo of the pillar sign, drop a map pin

problem: Street meters have a 2-hour cap and the driver has to physically return or re-pay while in the middle of work, or accept a ticket.
who: drivers parking for appointments and errands

problem: Service fees and event surcharges get added at checkout so the price on the sign or listing is never what you actually pay, making comparisons useless.

problem: A parking session keeps running or re-charges after the driver has left, and a $6 refund takes weeks of back-and-forth.

problem: Street parking permits expire, visitor passes run out, and guests get ticketed because renewal and issuing is a clunky city process nobody remembers.

source_quote: buses that show up on transit tracker apps but fail to arrive in real life

problem: Riders with strollers, wheelchairs or luggage arrive to find the only elevator broken, with outage information buried or not published.
workaround: check agency alerts page, ask staff

problem: The bus is routinely late so riders never know whether to wait, walk, or give up, and they end up leaving far earlier than needed as insurance.

problem: Real-time bus positions jump, disappear, and come back spontaneously, so riders cannot tell if the vehicle is two stops away or was pulled from service.
workaround: refresh repeatedly, compare two different apps
source_quote: buses appearing or disappearing from the tracker spontaneously

title: Missing the bus by seconds
problem: You check the arrival time, walk to the stop, and watch the doors close as you arrive because the prediction did not account for your walking time.
who: transit riders who check arrivals before leaving

problem: Predicted arrival times are off by many minutes or missing for entire routes, so riders stop trusting the app and revert to guessing.
workaround: use the printed schedule, ask other riders

problem: Delays, reroutes and platform changes are announced late, inconsistently, or only in-station, so commuters find out after they are already stuck.
workaround: follow agency social accounts, group chats with coworkers
source_quote: Delayed trains, unaffordable costs, and exhausting distances... unreliable real-time updates

problem: Drivers accept the trip, see the destination or wait for surge, then cancel, leaving the rider restarting the request and now late.
who: ride-hail riders, especially short or awkward trips

problem: A card decline or payment glitch cancels the request without a clear message, and sometimes money is held even though no ride was confirmed.

problem: Coworkers or friends share a ride-hail and then chase each other for their share, with tips and surge making the math awkward.
workaround: Venmo requests, letting it slide

problem: Commuters board packed vehicles with no way to know which run or which car will have space, so they get crushed or watch full vehicles pass.

problem: Seating, temperature and crowding vary wildly between cars and runs, and riders cannot tell before boarding where they will get a seat or a working AC.

title: Which door for the fastest exit
problem: Riders do not know which car and door lines up with the stairs at their exit station, so they lose minutes and miss connections.
workaround: memorize over months

title: Inconsistent sizing between brands
problem: A medium in one brand is a large in another, and nothing remembers which size fit last time from each store.

workaround: unsubscribing one at a time, throwaway email addresses

problem: People put off resolving billing errors or broken products because they expect to sit on hold for an hour, so problems linger unresolved.

problem: The driver never rings or even approaches the door, yet the tracking says 'attempted delivery' and the recipient has to chase a redelivery or pick up at a depot.

who: people receiving furniture, appliances or signature packages

problem: A subscription tied to an old email or lost login keeps charging because the company will not cancel without access to that account.

title: Loyalty points expiring unnoticed

who: shoppers enrolled in multiple loyalty programs

title: Product recalls go unnoticed
problem: Recalls for items already in the home (cribs, heaters, food) are announced but owners rarely hear about them because nobody connects purchases to recall notices.

title: Warranty expiry dates unknown
problem: By the time an appliance or gadget breaks, nobody remembers when it was bought or whether it is still under warranty, so claims are missed.

title: Receipts and manuals lost
problem: Paper receipts fade or get tossed, and product manuals vanish, so when something needs a return, warranty claim or repair the proof and instructions are gone.

title: Extended warranty worth-it decision

who: people with friends and family overseas

title: Keeping grandparents in the loop on kids

problem: Typing 'vets at 2pm' in a title auto-sets a time and adds an hour, so shared events end up wrong and someone shows up late.

who: extended families at Christmas and birthdays

title: No idea what to get someone

who: families, friend groups and offices at holidays

title: Gifting people you rarely see

title: Group vacations straining friendships

title: Deciding where to eat as a group

title: Tracking dietary restrictions across friends
problem: When hosting or booking, you have to remember who is vegan, gluten-free or allergic to nuts, and someone always gets forgotten.
workaround: ask again every time

title: Deciding a movie or game for the group
problem: Picking what to watch or play takes longer than the activity itself as everyone vetoes and nobody commits.
who: friends and families on a night in

title: Always being the one who initiates

title: Friendships fading from sheer busyness
problem: Jobs, partners and kids take over, months pass without a message, and a good friend becomes someone you 'should really call'.

title: Birthday reminders without meaningful contact

who: people with large, dispersed social circles

title: Remembering details people told you

who: anyone with many acquaintances or infrequent friends

title: Reminder apps feel like a chore list for friends

who: people who tried personal CRM apps
workaround: delete the app

title: Sharing photos after an outing
problem: Everyone took photos on their own phone and they never all end up in one place; the group asks 'can you send those pics?' for weeks.
who: friend groups and families after events

title: Collecting everyone's share for a group booking
