workaround: manual opt-outs, paid removal services

title: Old posts and accounts embarrass you years later
problem: Content from teenage years on forums and social media is still findable by employers and dates, and cleanup is per-post.
workaround: manual deletion, googling yourself

title: Wi-Fi password sharing with guests
problem: Guests ask for the Wi-Fi and the router password is a 20-character string on a sticker in a cupboard.
workaround: reading it aloud, photographing the sticker, QR code taped up

title: Doomscrolling in bed delays sleep
problem: Late-night scrolling pushes bedtime back and the phone is also the alarm, so it can't simply be left in another room.
workaround: bedtime mode, wind-down, willpower

title: Kids' screen limits negotiated per device
problem: Children's time is spread across tablet, console, TV and a friend's phone, and limits set on one device don't count the others.
workaround: verbal rules, separate parental controls per device

title: Opening the phone for one thing, losing 20 minutes
problem: You unlock to check the weather, get pulled into a feed, and forget what you came for.
workaround: notification purges, app timers

title: Screen time limits are trivially bypassed
problem: Built-in limits are dismissed with 'ignore for today' or 'one more minute', so they stop working within a week.
who: adults trying to cut phone use
workaround: grayscale mode, deleting apps, dumb phone

title: Notification overload from every app
problem: Dozens of apps send promotional pings, so real messages are buried and the reflex is to check the phone constantly.
workaround: muting apps one by one, Do Not Disturb

title: Screen-time reports don't distinguish useful from wasteful use
problem: Weekly reports lump maps, reading and work chat together with feeds, making the number meaningless and easy to ignore.
workaround: ignoring the report

title: 'Storage almost full' at the worst moment
problem: The phone refuses to take a photo or update because storage is full, and clearing space in the moment means deleting things blindly.
workaround: deleting apps and videos in a panic, 'offload' features

title: Battery dying earlier than expected each day
problem: Some app drains the battery in the background and identifying the culprit from the OS battery screen is confusing.
workaround: low power mode, uninstall guesses

title: Messaging app media fills the phone
problem: Auto-downloaded group-chat videos and forwarded memes quietly consume gigabytes, with cleanup buried deep in settings.
workaround: manual 'manage storage' cleanups

title: Mystery 'Other' or 'System' storage
problem: Tens of gigabytes are labelled Other/System with no way to see what they are or safely remove them.
workaround: factory reset, cache clearing guides

title: Old devices with data still on them
problem: Retired phones and laptops sit in a drawer with photos and logins on them, too risky to donate and too much work to wipe properly.
workaround: keeping them forever

title: Unused apps hog space and permissions
problem: Dozens of apps opened once still take space, send notifications and hold location and contacts permissions.
workaround: occasional purge, OS offload feature

title: Checking on a parent who lives alone
problem: Adult children worry an elderly parent has fallen and are reduced to calling several times a day, which the parent finds intrusive and the child finds exhausting.
who: adult children of elderly parents, people who live alone
workaround: Daily phone calls; medical alert pendants; neighbours

title: Living alone with no one to notice
problem: People who live alone fear that if they fell ill or were injured at home, days could pass before anyone realised something was wrong.
who: single adults, remote workers, people with health conditions
workaround: Arranging daily texts with a friend; none for most

title: Teen curfew tracking damages trust
problem: Parents want to know a teenager arrived at a friend's house safely, but constant location tracking causes fights and teens disable it.
workaround: Life360; demanding texts on arrival

title: Emergency contacts hidden behind lock screen
problem: If you collapse, bystanders or paramedics cannot see who to call or your allergies because the phone is locked and Medical ID is rarely set up or found.
who: everyone, especially people with medical conditions
workaround: Phone Medical ID; wallet card; medical bracelet

title: Kids' emergency info unavailable to sitters
problem: Babysitters and grandparents do not have the paediatrician's number, allergy list, insurance details and parents' whereabouts written anywhere when something goes wrong.
workaround: A note on the fridge; texting details each time

title: Lost phone means lost emergency numbers
problem: When your phone is lost or dead you cannot remember any contact's number, so you cannot call family from a borrowed phone.
who: everyone who relies on a smartphone contact list
workaround: Memorizing one number; a paper card in the wallet

title: Not knowing local emergency numbers abroad
problem: In a foreign country you do not know whether to dial 112, 911 or 999, what the poison line is, or where the nearest embassy and hospital are.
workaround: Searching online in the moment; hotel front desk

title: Emergency contact list goes stale
problem: The 'in case of emergency' contacts on your phone, work HR form and gym membership list an ex-partner or an old number, and nobody remembers to update them.
who: adults after a move, breakup or family change
workaround: none

title: No clear path to report scams
problem: After a phishing text, stalker message or suspicious visitor, people do not know which agency or platform to report to and give up.
workaround: Blocking the number; posting a warning to friends

title: Important documents inaccessible when evacuating
problem: Fleeing a fire or flood you cannot grab insurance policies, IDs and medication lists, and later you have no copies to file claims with.
who: households in wildfire, hurricane or flood zones
workaround: A folder in a closet; scattered cloud drive photos

title: Emergency kit supplies expire unnoticed
problem: Water, food, batteries and medicines in the go-bag or car kit quietly pass their expiry dates, so the kit is useless when finally needed.
who: households that keep emergency kits, preppers, drivers
workaround: Calendar reminder once a year; checking during daylight-saving changes

title: Power outage leaves you uninformed
problem: When the power goes out you cannot tell whether it is just your house, how large the outage is, or when it will be restored, and the utility's status page is hard to reach on mobile data.
workaround: Utility outage map; neighbourhood group chat

title: Weather alerts too broad or too many
problem: Government weather and emergency alerts cover a whole county, so residents get woken for events far away and then silence alerts before the one that matters.
who: residents of storm, flood and wildfire regions
workaround: Multiple weather apps; local news; turning alerts off

title: Explaining where you are to dispatch
problem: On a highway, trail or in a large building you cannot give a useful address to the emergency operator and waste critical minutes describing landmarks.
who: drivers, hikers, people in unfamiliar places
workaround: Reading GPS coordinates from a map app; what3words

title: Family cannot reach each other in a disaster
problem: During an earthquake, storm or outage the network is jammed, and nobody agreed in advance where to meet or who checks in with whom.
workaround: Red Cross 'safe and well' pages; group texts that fail

title: Forgetting what to do in a medical emergency
problem: When someone chokes, has a seizure or a suspected stroke, panic makes people forget the basic steps they learned in a first-aid course years ago.
workaround: Calling emergency services and following the operator; Red Cross app

title: Lost child in a crowded place
problem: At a fair, mall or beach a child wanders off and the parent has no current photo of what they are wearing, no venue contact and no plan agreed with the child.
workaround: Taking a photo at the entrance; writing a phone number on the child's arm

title: Car breakdown on a road with no plan
problem: When the car dies at night you scramble to find the roadside assistance number, your policy number and a way to tell someone exactly where you are.
workaround: Insurance card in the glovebox; searching online

title: Deciding if a symptom is an emergency
problem: At 2am you cannot tell whether chest tightness, a child's fever or a deep cut warrants the ER, urgent care or waiting until morning, and the phone lines have long holds.
who: parents, caregivers, anyone without a doctor on call
workaround: Nurse hotlines; Googling symptoms; going to the ER to be safe

title: Package theft from the porch
problem: Deliveries left on the doorstep disappear before you get home, and coordinating delivery windows or a safe drop spot with each carrier is unreliable.
who: online shoppers in apartments and busy streets
workaround: Delivering to work or lockers; asking neighbours to grab parcels

title: Security camera notification overload
problem: Doorbell and yard cameras ping for every passing car, cat and shadow, so dozens of daily alerts bury the one real intruder event.
who: owners of doorbell and home cameras
workaround: Motion zones; disabling notifications; paid AI person-detection tiers

title: Uncertainty whether door locked, stove off
problem: Halfway to work you cannot remember whether the front door is locked, the garage closed or the iron off, and turn back or worry all day.
who: commuters, people with anxiety or OCD
workaround: Photo of the locked door; smart locks; saying it aloud

title: Empty home looks empty while away
problem: On vacation the house is dark, mail piles up and bins are not put out, signalling to burglars that nobody is home, and asking neighbours for each task is awkward.
workaround: Timer plugs; mail hold; asking a neighbour

title: Fire and CO alarm testing forgotten
problem: Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors need monthly tests and battery changes, and expire after ten years, but nobody tracks when each unit was installed or checked.
workaround: Change batteries when the clocks change; wait for the chirp

title: Neighbourhood crime info is rumour-driven
problem: Residents hear about break-ins and car thefts via alarmist group posts, with no reliable view of what actually happened on their street this month.
who: residents in suburbs and city neighbourhoods
workaround: Nextdoor and neighbourhood WhatsApp groups; police blotters

title: Security gear split across many apps
problem: The doorbell, indoor cameras, smart lock and alarm each have their own app and login, so checking the house means opening four apps and no one gets a single 'all secure' view.
workaround: Sticking to one brand; home automation hubs for technical users

title: Temporary access for guests and workers
problem: Giving a cleaner, dog walker or contractor access means handing out physical keys or sharing the alarm code, with no record of who came in when and no easy way to revoke.
workaround: Lockboxes; spare keys under mats; smart lock codes

title: Who has the keys and codes
problem: In a household several people hold spare keys, know the alarm code and the safe combination, and when one is lost or a relationship ends nobody knows what needs changing.
workaround: none

title: Lost pet search is chaotic
problem: When a dog or cat goes missing the owner must post in many neighbourhood groups, print flyers, call shelters and vets separately, all while panicking.
workaround: Facebook groups, Nextdoor, paper flyers, calling shelters

title: Wallet theft recovery steps are scattered
problem: After a theft you must freeze cards, order a new license, file a police report and watch for fraud, but there is no ordered checklist with the right phone numbers and deadlines for your cards and country.
workaround: Google searches while stressed; calling each bank

title: Airline lost luggage tracking is opaque
problem: Delayed bags require a reference number, repeated calls and a claim form, with no clear status on where the bag is or when it will be delivered.
workaround: AirTag in the suitcase; calling the airline daily

title: Leaving items behind in rideshares
problem: You realize hours later that your phone, umbrella or bag stayed in the Uber or taxi, and reaching the driver means digging through the app for a support form with slow replies.
workaround: Rideshare 'lost item' form; calling the driver via masked number for a fee

title: No single place to report a lost item
problem: When you lose something in a city you have to guess whether it went to the bus company, the venue, the police or a nearby cafe, and each has its own form, phone line or none at all.
workaround: Calling each place; posting on local Facebook groups

title: Not knowing what was in a lost bag
problem: After a bag or wallet goes missing you cannot recall exactly which cards, IDs and documents were inside, so you do not know what to cancel or replace.
who: anyone who has lost a wallet, purse or backpack
workaround: Scrolling old bank statements and photos; guessing

title: Proving ownership of recovered items
problem: When a stolen bike or laptop turns up, police or the pawn shop ask for serial numbers and receipts you never recorded.
workaround: Searching email for the receipt; photos of the item

title: Finders cannot contact the owner
problem: Someone picks up a set of keys, a wallet or a water bottle but has no way to reach the owner, so the item ends up in a drawer or the trash.
who: anyone who finds or loses items in public
workaround: Hand to nearest staff; post a photo on social media

title: Forgetting items when leaving a place
problem: Chargers stay in hotel rooms, jackets at restaurants and sunglasses at friends' houses because there is no reminder to check your belongings before walking out.
workaround: Mental 'phone, wallet, keys' check; packing lists

title: Kids' belongings vanish at school
problem: Water bottles, lunch boxes, hoodies and PE kit disappear weekly and parents have no way to see the school's lost-and-found pile without visiting in person.
workaround: Labelling everything; asking teachers by email

title: Bluetooth tracker alerts fire too often
problem: Item trackers send 'left behind' alerts every time you walk to the mailbox or leave keys at home deliberately, so you start ignoring them and miss the real one.
workaround: Turning off alerts; setting trusted locations one by one

title: Forgetting where you stored rarely used things
problem: Passport, spare keys, warranty cards or the holiday decorations were put somewhere 'safe' months ago and now nobody can remember which box, drawer or closet.
who: households, movers, people with storage units
workaround: Searching every closet; asking family in a group chat

title: Keys, wallet, phone misplaced at home
problem: Several times a week you leave the house late because your keys, wallet or phone are not where you thought you put them, and you have no way to know which room to search first.
who: almost everyone, especially people with ADHD or busy households
workaround: Bluetooth trackers on some items; retracing steps; a bowl by the door

title: Trackers from different brands in separate apps
problem: A household with AirTags, Tiles and Samsung tags must open three apps to check items, and one partner's Android phone cannot see the other's Apple tags at all.
workaround: Buying only one brand; sharing screenshots

title: Lent items never come back
problem: Books, tools, cables and cash lent to friends and colleagues are forgotten by both sides, and asking months later feels awkward because nobody is sure who has what.
workaround: Notes app; just accepting the loss

title: Discreet SOS without unlocking the phone
problem: In a threatening moment you cannot unlock the phone, open an app and type; you need one hidden gesture that alerts chosen people with your location.
who: people in unsafe situations, domestic abuse survivors
workaround: Phone power-button emergency SOS, which calls 911 rather than a friend

title: Fake call excuse to leave a situation
problem: On a bad date or when someone is following you, you want a believable interruption that gives you a reason to walk away without escalating.
who: people on first dates, solo travelers, women walking alone
workaround: Texting a friend to call; pretending to answer the phone

title: Meeting strangers from online listings
problem: Buying from marketplace listings or meeting a date means going to a stranger's location with nobody knowing the address, time or the person's details.
who: online marketplace buyers and sellers, online daters
workaround: Screenshotting the profile to a friend; meeting at police station lots

title: No one knows you got home safe
problem: Walking home late you want someone to know when you arrive, but texting a friend at 1am is awkward and they may be asleep and not notice if you never text.
who: students, shift workers, people walking alone at night
workaround: Texting 'home' to a friend; staying on the phone

title: Phone dies during a night out
problem: A dead phone late at night leaves you unable to call a ride, reach friends or navigate, and friends cannot find you either.
who: young adults, festival and concert goers
workaround: Power banks; agreeing a meeting point in advance

title: Running or hiking alone unmonitored
problem: Solo runners and hikers may fall or get lost with nobody expecting them back at a set time, and their phone may have no signal to call.
workaround: Telling a partner the route; satellite messengers for serious hikers

title: Choosing a safer walking route at night
problem: Map apps pick the fastest route, which may go through unlit parks or empty streets; there is no way to prefer well-lit, busy streets after dark.
workaround: Sticking to main roads from memory; taking a taxi

title: Rideshare driver mismatch anxiety
problem: Getting into the wrong car is a real worry at night; checking plate, model and driver photo in a rush is easy to skip.
workaround: Asking the driver 'who are you here for'; sharing trip status

title: Sharing live location drains battery
problem: Keeping location sharing on for safety uses so much battery that the phone dies exactly when you would need it, so people turn it off.
who: users of Find My and Life360 style apps
workaround: Sharing only for short trips; carrying a power bank

title: Client passwords shared unsafely
problem: Clients send website, hosting and social media passwords over email or text, and freelancers store them in notes files.
workaround: notes app, password manager

title: Contracts signed by screenshot or not at all
problem: Getting a proper signed agreement feels heavy, so work starts on a handshake and disputes have no paper trail.
workaround: PDF via email, DocuSign trial

title: Subcontractor payments and hours
problem: Farming out work to another freelancer means tracking their hours, invoices, and paying them on time from the client's payment.
who: small agencies and freelancers who subcontract
workaround: spreadsheet

title: Subscription creep for business tools
problem: A dozen SaaS tools at $10-30 each pile up, some unused, and nobody reviews them.
workaround: check bank statement occasionally

title: Retyping answers to the same client questions
problem: Every client asks about turnaround time, payment terms, and revision policy, and the answers are retyped every time.
workaround: canned email snippets

title: Quarterly estimated taxes are a surprise
problem: Freelancers don't know how much to set aside and get hit with a large tax bill and penalties each quarter or year.
who: self-employed in the US and similar
workaround: set aside a rough percentage

title: Income from many platforms hard to total
problem: Money arrives via PayPal, Stripe, Upwork, Etsy, and bank transfers, and getting a true monthly income figure means logging into five dashboards.
workaround: spreadsheet

title: Mixed personal and business transactions
problem: Business expenses paid from a personal card and vice versa make it painful to separate what is deductible.
workaround: manually tag bank transactions

title: Receipts piling up unsorted
problem: Paper and email receipts accumulate for months and get sorted in a panic at tax time, with many lost or faded.
workaround: shoebox, photos in camera roll

title: Sales tax or VAT across jurisdictions
problem: Selling to clients in different states or countries raises the question of whether to charge sales tax or VAT, at what rate, and when to file.
workaround: ignore it or ask an accountant

title: Unclear whether the business is profitable
problem: Revenue feels fine but after software subscriptions, fees, and taxes it's unclear what the real take-home is per month or per client.
workaround: annual accountant summary

title: Home office expense apportioning
problem: Working out what share of rent, internet, and phone counts as a business expense is confusing and redone every year.
workaround: guess a percentage

title: Invoices and bank deposits don't match
problem: Reconciling which deposit corresponds to which invoice, after fees and partial payments, takes hours each month.
workaround: manual matching in spreadsheet

title: Mileage tracking forgotten
problem: Business driving is deductible but logging trips manually is tedious, so most trips go unrecorded.
workaround: notebook, rough estimate

title: Tax forms from many clients
problem: Collecting 1099-type forms from each client, or issuing them to subcontractors, involves chasing and tracking dozens of documents every January.
workaround: email reminders, folder

title: Client feedback scattered across channels
problem: Feedback arrives via email, WhatsApp, text, Slack and phone calls, so revision requests get missed or contradict each other.
workaround: copy everything into one doc

title: Endless revision rounds
problem: Contracts allow two revisions but nobody tracks the count, and clients keep sending 'one more small change' indefinitely.
workaround: manual counting, arguing

title: Waiting on client assets and content
problem: Projects stall because the client has not sent logos, copy, or logins, and it is unclear who is blocking whom.
workaround: nagging emails

title: Clients ignoring working hours
problem: Clients text and call at night and on weekends expecting instant replies, and there is no polite automated boundary.
workaround: mute phone, autoresponder

title: Ghosted mid-project
problem: A client disappears after work has started, and there is no clear process for pausing, billing partial work, or closing out.
workaround: send a few emails then give up

title: No single view of client history
problem: Past projects, rates agreed, preferences, and contact people for each client live in memory or scattered files, so returning clients feel like strangers.
workaround: spreadsheet, email search

title: Onboarding questionnaire chaos
problem: Collecting brand details, access, goals and preferences from a new client happens over many emails and is never in one place.
workaround: Google Form, email list

title: Sharing large files and getting sign-off
problem: Sending deliverables via WeTransfer links that expire, then chasing a formal 'approved' response, drags on final delivery.
workaround: Dropbox, email 'looks good'

title: Income too irregular to budget
problem: Feast-or-famine months make it impossible to know whether a slow month is a crisis or normal, or how much can be safely paid out.
workaround: big emergency buffer, anxiety

title: Gig platform fees hidden in earnings
problem: Platform take rates change and are buried in statements, so workers don't know their true hourly rate after fees, mileage and time waiting.
workaround: rough math

title: Juggling several gig apps at once
problem: Drivers and taskers run Uber, DoorDash, Instacart simultaneously and can't easily compare which app is paying best right now or track combined earnings.
workaround: switch between apps, notebook

title: Marketplace order fulfillment tracking
problem: Small sellers lose track of which orders are made, packed, shipped, and which customers messaged about delays.
workaround: platform dashboard, sticky notes

title: Supplies and materials running out
problem: Makers and small sellers run out of a key material mid-order because supply levels and reorder points are not tracked.
workaround: eyeballing the shelf

title: Tracking marketplace proposals sent
problem: Winning work on Upwork or Fiverr requires sending many proposals, and tracking which ones were viewed, replied to, or hired is chaotic.
workaround: platform inbox, spreadsheet

title: Side hustle time competing with day job
problem: A side hustle gets random evening hours and there is no way to see whether the time invested is worth the money earned.
workaround: none

title: Chasing overdue invoices by hand
problem: Freelancers spend hours every month writing awkward reminder emails for invoices that are 30, 60, 90 days late, and lose track of which client has been nudged how many times.
workaround: manual email follow-ups, spreadsheet of due dates

title: Clients disputing hours after the fact
problem: When an hourly invoice arrives the client questions what took so long, and the freelancer has no clear per-task breakdown to back it up.
workaround: vague time logs, memory

title: Forgetting to invoice small add-ons
problem: Small extra requests done mid-project ('can you just tweak this') never get logged, so they are never billed and revenue leaks away.
workaround: memory, sticky notes

title: Milestone payments tracked by memory
problem: On a multi-milestone project it becomes unclear what percentage has been paid, what is outstanding, and which deliverable unlocks the next payment.
workaround: spreadsheet per project

title: Check and wire payments with surprise fees
problem: Clients pay via methods that take weeks to clear or deduct wire and processing fees, so the amount received never matches the invoice and reconciling is a headache.
who: freelancers with corporate or overseas clients
workaround: eat the fee, manually adjust in books

title: Late-fee terms never enforced
problem: Contracts say 'late fees apply' but calculating and adding them requires manual work and an awkward conversation, so they are never charged.
workaround: none

title: Multi-currency invoices and exchange losses
problem: Billing an overseas client means guessing the exchange rate, losing money on conversion, and then not knowing what to record as income in home currency.
workaround: Wise/PayPal, manual conversion in spreadsheet

title: Not knowing if an invoice was opened
problem: After sending an invoice you have no idea whether the client saw it, forwarded it to accounting, or it went to spam, so you can't tell when to follow up.
workaround: ask the client, wait and hope

title: Processor fees eating small invoices
problem: Card processing fees of 3% plus a fixed amount make small invoices barely worth sending, and deciding whether to pass fees on to the client is confusing.
workaround: add a surcharge line or absorb it

title: Recurring retainer invoices sent late
problem: Monthly retainer invoices depend on the freelancer remembering to generate and send them on the 1st, and forgetting delays cash flow by weeks.
workaround: calendar reminder, copy last month's invoice

title: Following up with leads inconsistently
problem: Prospects who said 'maybe next quarter' are forgotten because there is no lightweight way to schedule a nudge.
workaround: CRM too heavy, memory

title: Collecting testimonials and reviews
problem: Happy clients rarely leave a review unless asked at the right moment, and asking is awkward and forgotten.
workaround: occasional email ask

title: Not knowing where clients come from
problem: Referrals, social media, marketplaces and cold outreach all bring work, but nobody records which source actually converts.
workaround: guess

title: Portfolio always out of date
problem: Finished work never gets added to the portfolio or website because it takes effort to write it up and get client permission.
workaround: batch update once a year

title: Scope creep with no change-order process
problem: Clients ask for 'small additions' beyond the agreed scope and, without a quick way to price and document extras, the freelancer either does them free or argues.
workaround: awkward email negotiations

title: Approval is a vague 'sounds good' email
problem: Work starts on a casual 'go ahead' reply with no formal sign-off on scope, price, or terms, which creates disputes later.
workaround: screenshot the email

title: Not knowing what to charge
problem: New freelancers have no idea whether their hourly or project rate is reasonable for their skill, market and region, and rarely revisit it as they improve.
workaround: asking peers, Reddit threads

title: Quotes going stale without follow-up
problem: A quote is sent, the prospect goes silent, and there is no system to know how many quotes are open, their value, or when to check in.
workaround: spreadsheet or memory

title: Rewriting the same proposal from scratch
problem: Every proposal starts from a blank document or an old one with the wrong client name, and hours go into formatting instead of selling.
workaround: Word template, find-and-replace

title: Underquoting from unknown past project time
problem: Quoting a new job means guessing how long it will take, because nobody records how long similar past projects actually took versus what was quoted.
workaround: gut feeling, rounding up

title: Hourly versus project pricing confusion
problem: Deciding whether to bill hourly, per-project, or per-value on each job, and translating one into the other, is done ad hoc and leads to inconsistent pricing.
workaround: none

title: Quote versions lost in email threads
problem: Revised quotes go back and forth by email and nobody is sure which version the client actually approved.
workaround: search email, ask client

title: Last-minute cancellations and no-shows
problem: Clients cancel an hour before or simply don't show, wasting slots that can't be refilled and costing income.
workaround: deposit policy, texting reminders manually

title: Capacity unknown when accepting new work
problem: Saying yes to a new project without knowing how many hours are already committed next month leads to overbooking and burnout.
workaround: rough mental estimate

title: Double-booking across multiple calendars
problem: Personal, work and client calendars are not synced, so consultations get booked over each other or over personal commitments.
workaround: Calendly plus manual checks

title: Travel time missing from the schedule
problem: Mobile service businesses book appointments without accounting for driving time between jobs, causing lateness and dead time.
workaround: guess a buffer

title: Back-and-forth to find a meeting time
problem: Five emails to agree on a time for a 20-minute call, repeated for every prospect and client.
workaround: scheduling links

title: Recurring client appointments drifting
problem: Standing weekly or monthly bookings slip when someone reschedules once and the recurrence is never re-established.
workaround: manual re-entry

title: Time zone mistakes with remote clients
problem: Scheduling calls with clients in other time zones leads to missed meetings because someone converted the time wrong.
workaround: world clock, asking twice

title: Too many small projects to track
problem: With eight clients and twelve small projects, deadlines and next steps are tracked in heads and inboxes, and something slips every week.
workaround: Trello, notebook

title: Deadlines promised without seeing workload
problem: Promising a delivery date on Friday without seeing that three other deadlines fall the same week.
workaround: calendar glance

title: Forgetting to start or stop the timer
problem: Hourly work goes unbilled or over-billed because timers are started late or left running overnight.
workaround: estimate afterward

title: Unpaid admin time invisible
problem: Emails, invoicing, and calls take a big chunk of the week but are never measured, so effective hourly rate is far lower than believed.
workaround: none

title: Campus email overload
problem: The university sends dozens of newsletters, reminders, and announcements daily, and the one important message about a registration hold is buried.
workaround: ignoring the inbox and missing things

title: Making friends as a transfer or commuter
problem: Students who don't live in dorms or arrived after freshman year have no natural way to meet people and feel isolated.
workaround: joining clubs at random

title: Finding a ride home for breaks
problem: Students without cars need rides to the airport or hometown at holiday breaks and rely on chance posts to find someone going the same way.
workaround: Facebook rideshare groups and expensive Ubers

title: Hearing about campus events after they happen
problem: Club meetings, free food events, and guest talks are announced on flyers and in emails students never read, so they find out the next day.
workaround: Instagram follows and a bloated inbox

title: Lost campus printing and parking rules
problem: Students don't know where they can print, how many pages are free, or which lot they can park in without a ticket.
workaround: asking around and getting fined

title: Missing the campus shuttle
problem: Shuttle and campus bus times are unreliable, and students either wait 20 minutes in the cold or watch it leave as they arrive.
who: students on large or multi-campus universities
workaround: leaving far too early, or walking

title: Dining hall menu and crowding unknown
problem: Students walk across campus to a dining hall only to find a menu they don't want or a 30-minute line.
workaround: checking a PDF menu that's often outdated

title: Gym and rec center overcrowded
problem: Students show up to the campus gym at peak time and every rack and treadmill is taken.
workaround: guessing off-peak hours

title: Registration holds discovered on registration day
problem: A missing immunization form or an unpaid $15 fee blocks course registration and the student finds out when the classes fill.
workaround: checking the portal repeatedly the week before

title: Tracking internship applications
problem: Students apply to 50+ internships with different deadlines, portals, and follow-up steps and lose track of where each stands.
workaround: a spreadsheet that gets abandoned

title: Forgetting to log volunteer or co-curricular hours
problem: Programs and scholarships require documented hours, and students reconstruct months of activity from memory at the deadline.
who: students in honors, service, or scholarship programs
workaround: guessing and hoping no one checks

title: Keeping citations formatted correctly
problem: Every paper needs APA or MLA citations, and students lose points on formatting or spend hours fixing reference lists.
workaround: Zotero, citation generators with wrong output

title: Waitlisted class seat opens unnoticed
problem: A seat in a full required class opens for a few hours and is gone again before the student happens to refresh the registration page.
workaround: refreshing the enrollment page dozens of times a day

title: Building a conflict-free class schedule
problem: Choosing sections that satisfy degree requirements, avoid time overlaps, avoid 8 AM slots, and leave gaps for work takes hours of trial and error.
workaround: paper grids, multiple browser tabs, and screenshots of the catalog

title: Degree requirements progress is opaque
problem: Students can't easily see which requirements are complete, which courses double-count, and whether they'll graduate on time, until an advisor meeting months away.
workaround: a printed degree audit and a hand-maintained checklist

title: Not knowing current grade in a class
problem: Weighted categories, dropped lowest scores, and ungraded items make it impossible to tell whether a student is at a B+ or a C, so they can't decide where to focus.
who: students tracking GPA or scholarship thresholds
workaround: building a spreadsheet from the syllabus weighting, often wrong

title: Choosing professors with no reliable info
problem: Students pick sections blind, relying on outdated or gamed rating sites, and end up with a grader or teaching style that wrecks their term.
workaround: asking friends and reading Rate My Professors

title: What score is needed on the final
problem: Before the final exam students want to know the minimum score to keep their letter grade, and have to recompute weights by hand every time.
workaround: generic 'final grade calculator' websites that ignore dropped scores

title: Deadlines scattered across five course platforms
problem: Each course posts assignments in a different place (Canvas, a professor's website, email, a syllabus PDF), so students miss due dates they never saw in one list.
workaround: manually copying every syllabus into a calendar or notes app at the start of term

title: Three exams landing in the same week
problem: Students only realize in week 9 that midterms for three classes fall within two days, leaving no time to study for each properly.
workaround: cramming, or asking a professor for an extension after the fact

title: Big assignment not broken into steps
problem: A 20-page paper due in six weeks feels unstartable, so nothing happens until three days before and the whole thing is written in a panic.
workaround: all-nighters; vague intentions to 'start early'

title: Missing the 11:59 PM submission cutoff
problem: Uploads at 11:58 fail because the file is too large or the portal is slow, and the assignment is marked late by a minute.
who: students who work up to the deadline
workaround: screenshotting the upload error as evidence for the professor

title: Submitting the wrong file version
problem: Students upload a draft instead of the final, or the wrong file entirely, and only notice after the portal locks.
workaround: emailing the professor begging to resubmit

title: Syllabus dates changed mid-semester
problem: Professors shift due dates verbally in class or in a buried announcement, so the calendar the student built in week one is quietly wrong.
who: students who plan from the syllabus
workaround: asking classmates in the group chat 'wait, is that still due Friday?'

title: Wasting the gaps between classes
problem: Students have scattered 50-minute gaps across the day that are too short to go home and end up scrolling instead of working.
workaround: none

title: Finding a compatible roommate or subletter
problem: Students need a roommate for next year or someone to take their lease over summer, and matching happens through random Facebook posts with strangers.
workaround: Facebook housing groups and campus bulletin boards

title: Laundry machines all taken
problem: Students haul laundry down to the basement to find every machine in use, or return to find their clothes dumped on the floor.
workaround: going at 6 AM; some campuses have machine-status apps that rarely work

title: Moving out every summer
problem: Students must pack, store, and move everything they own every May and August, and forget what's in storage or what they need to buy again.
workaround: storage companies and a pile of unlabeled boxes

title: Roommate chores never get done
problem: Dishes pile up, trash overflows, and the bathroom goes uncleaned because nobody agreed on whose turn it is.
who: students in dorms and shared apartments
workaround: passive-aggressive notes and one person doing everything

title: Roommate schedule and quiet hours clash
problem: One roommate has an 8 AM class and the other games until 3 AM; neither knows the other's schedule so conflicts happen daily.
workaround: arguments or a whiteboard on the door

title: Dorm maintenance requests vanish
problem: A broken heater or leaking sink is reported through a clunky portal and no one knows if or when it will be fixed.
workaround: reporting again, or bothering the RA

title: Shared groceries disappear from the fridge
problem: Food bought by one roommate is eaten by another, and nobody tracks what is shared versus personal.
workaround: labels with names on them; mini-fridge in the bedroom

title: Group member goes silent before deadline
problem: One teammate stops responding days before the due date, and the rest have no idea whether their part is coming or must be redone.
workaround: frantic messages, then doing the work themselves at 2 AM

title: Finding a meeting time for six people
problem: Coordinating a group meeting across six class schedules, jobs, and time zones takes a week of back-and-forth polls.
workaround: When2meet links and endless 'does Tuesday work?' messages

title: No record of who actually contributed
problem: When peer evaluations come, students can't prove a freeloader did nothing, and the freeloader gets the same grade.
workaround: screenshots of the group chat sent to the professor

title: Unclear who is doing which part
problem: Group projects are divided verbally in one meeting, then two people do the same section while a third section is forgotten.
workaround: a pinned message in the group chat nobody rereads

title: Group chat scattered across apps
problem: One group uses iMessage, another WhatsApp, another Discord, another Slack, and important messages and files get lost between them.
who: students in multiple groups per term
workaround: searching four apps to find the file someone sent

title: Merging five different document versions
problem: Each member writes their section in a different tool and format, and someone spends the last night stitching them into one consistent document.
workaround: one person copy-pasting everything into a single Google Doc

title: Counseling center booked out for weeks
problem: When stress peaks during exams, the campus counseling center has a three-week wait and students don't know other options.
workaround: friends, or nothing

title: Sleep schedule wrecked by late nights
problem: Assignments and social life push bedtime to 3 AM, then students sleep through 9 AM lectures and fall behind.
workaround: energy drinks and five alarms

title: Eating badly on a student budget
problem: Students with tiny kitchens, no time, and little money end up on instant noodles and takeout, and don't know cheap easy meals.
workaround: same three meals on repeat

title: Running out of money before month end
problem: Loan or allowance money arrives in a lump and is gone by week three, leaving students eating ramen until the next disbursement.
who: students on loans, stipends, or allowances
workaround: vague mental budgeting; borrowing from friends

title: Textbooks cost hundreds per term
problem: Required textbooks cost $100-300 each, and students don't know until week two whether the professor will actually use them.
workaround: pirated PDFs, library reserves, older editions, or skipping the book

title: Balancing part-time shifts with classes
problem: Work schedules change weekly and collide with labs, exams, and study time, and the student has no single view to spot the conflicts.
workaround: two separate calendars and hoping

title: Scholarship deadlines slip by
problem: Dozens of small scholarships have different deadlines and requirements, and students miss most of them because tracking is too much work.
workaround: a bookmarked list that is never revisited

title: Splitting costs with roommates
problem: Rent, utilities, toilet paper, and shared groceries are paid by whoever happened to be there, and nobody knows who owes whom.
workaround: Splitwise, Venmo requests, or letting it slide and resenting it

title: Reselling used textbooks for almost nothing
problem: Bookstore buyback pays a fraction of the price while other students on campus would pay more, but there's no easy way to match them.
workaround: Facebook groups and taped flyers

title: Unexpected university fees on the bill
problem: Tuition statements include lab fees, tech fees, and health fees the student never saw coming, and it's unclear which can be waived.
workaround: calling the bursar's office and waiting on hold

title: Unused meal plan swipes expire
problem: Students pay for meal plans, then lose dozens of swipes or dining dollars at the end of each week or semester.
workaround: buying cases of snacks in the last week, or giving swipes away

title: Finding which student discounts apply
problem: Software, transit, streaming, and local businesses offer student discounts, but students only find out by accident after paying full price.
workaround: UNiDAYS and word of mouth

title: Finding an empty study spot
problem: During midterms every library seat, study room, and outlet is taken, and students wander between buildings for half an hour.
workaround: arriving at 7 AM or texting friends to hold a seat

title: No practice problems for this specific course
problem: Textbook problems don't match what the professor tests, and past exams are hoarded or unavailable.
workaround: Chegg, frat test banks, or begging older students

title: Phone distraction during study sessions
problem: Students sit down to study and lose an hour to TikTok and group chats without noticing.
workaround: Forest app, phone in another room, or nothing

title: Booking a library study room
problem: Study room reservation systems are clunky, rooms get no-showed and sit empty while others are locked out.
workaround: squatting in rooms and hoping the booker doesn't show

title: Can't find a study partner for a class
problem: Students in a hard class don't know anyone in it and have no way to find others who want to study together.
workaround: awkwardly asking neighbors in lecture or posting in a Discord

title: Lecture notes hard to review later
problem: Handwritten and typed notes from a fast lecture are disorganized, incomplete, and impossible to search when it's time to study.
workaround: borrowing a friend's notes or rewatching the recorded lecture

title: Making flashcards eats study time
problem: Turning slides and readings into flashcards takes so long that students run out of time to actually review them.
who: students in memorization-heavy courses (bio, languages, law)
workaround: Quizlet sets made by strangers that don't match the course

title: Office hours conflict with other classes
problem: The only time a student can get help from a professor or TA overlaps another class or a shift, so questions go unanswered for weeks.
workaround: long email threads or Piazza posts that get answered late

title: Reading load impossible to plan
problem: Weekly reading assignments across courses add up to hundreds of pages and students can't judge how long each will take.
workaround: skimming or skipping readings

title: Recorded lectures too long to rewatch
problem: Reviewing for an exam means scrubbing through hours of 75-minute recordings to find the one part that was confusing.
who: students in courses with recorded lectures
workaround: watching at 2x speed

title: Getting to appointments without a car
problem: An elderly parent cannot drive, the caregiver works, and every appointment turns into a puzzle of who takes time off or how to arrange a ride.
who: caregivers of non-driving relatives, patients on sedating meds
workaround: taking unpaid leave, rideshares, volunteer driver programs

title: Phone-only booking during work hours
problem: The clinic can only be reached by phone between 9 and 4, the hold time is 30 minutes, and the patient is at work and cannot stay on the line.
workaround: calling on lunch break, using speakerphone at the desk

title: Referral status in limbo
problem: The GP says a referral was sent, the specialist says nothing arrived, and weeks pass with no one accountable for where it is.
workaround: calling both offices repeatedly

title: Remembering what the doctor said
problem: Half of the instructions given during the appointment are forgotten by the time the patient gets home, and the after-visit summary is vague or missing.
who: patients, especially elderly or anxious ones
workaround: bringing a relative to take notes, recording on the phone if allowed

title: Specialist waits stretching months
problem: The next available appointment is five months out, and there is no way to be notified when an earlier cancellation slot opens up.
who: anyone waiting on a specialist referral
workaround: calling the office every few days asking about cancellations

title: Juggling appointments across many providers
problem: Rheumatology, physio, bloodwork, dentist and GP all book separately, and the patient ends up with two visits in one week and none the next month, or a clash.
who: patients with multiple specialists, caregivers managing a parent's care
workaround: a shared Google calendar, a paper diary

title: Pre-appointment prep requirements
problem: Some tests require fasting, stopping a medication, or bringing specific documents, and the instruction sheet is lost by the time the day arrives.
who: patients scheduling lab work, scopes, imaging
workaround: rereading the letter, calling the clinic the day before

title: Recurring lab draws and screenings slipping
problem: Quarterly thyroid or A1c checks, annual eye exams and repeat scans have no fixed appointment and get forgotten until the doctor asks why it was not done.
who: patients with conditions requiring periodic monitoring
workaround: relying on the clinic to call, sticky notes

title: Caregiver burnout with no time off
problem: Full-time caregivers go months without a break because arranging respite care means finding, vetting and briefing someone, which is itself exhausting.
who: spouses and adult children caring full-time
workaround: relying on relatives, skipping breaks entirely

title: Handing off to a paid or relief caregiver
problem: When a home aide or relative takes over for a shift, they do not know what was given, eaten, or observed earlier that day, and details are lost in the handoff.
who: families using rotating carers or home health aides
workaround: a notebook on the kitchen counter, texts

title: Managing a parent's affairs as proxy
problem: Acting for a parent means juggling their portal logins, insurance calls where the office will not talk to you, POA paperwork and utility bills, on top of your own life.
who: adult children with power of attorney or healthcare proxy
workaround: folders of documents, calling with the parent on the line

title: Managing a parent's meds from far away
problem: A long-distance caregiver cannot tell whether their parent took today's pills, and the parent insists they did even when the organizer says otherwise.
workaround: daily phone calls, automatic dispensers, neighbors checking in

title: Siblings out of sync on a parent's care
problem: One sibling does most of the caregiving while the others ask 'how is Mom' in a group chat, and no one knows who spoke to which doctor or what was decided.
who: adult children sharing care of an aging parent
workaround: WhatsApp groups, shared notes, phone-call relays

title: Coordinating friends who want to help
problem: After a diagnosis, people offer to help but the patient has no energy to organize meals, rides and visits, so offers go unused while needs go unmet.
who: patients in cancer treatment, post-surgery recovery, new caregivers
workaround: meal-train sites, a friend acting as coordinator

title: Repeating updates to everyone who asks
problem: After each appointment or hospital day the caregiver retells the same news to a dozen relatives and friends individually, which is draining during a crisis.
who: caregivers and patients during acute illness
workaround: group texts, CaringBridge-style pages, one designated relay person

title: Tracking home-care agency hours and quality
problem: Families paying for in-home aides cannot easily verify which shifts were actually worked, who showed up, or what was done, and disputes with the agency follow.
workaround: sign-in sheets, cameras, asking the parent

title: Emergency info not reachable in a crisis
problem: When paramedics arrive, no one can quickly produce the patient's conditions, allergies, medications, DNR status and emergency contacts.
who: patients with complex conditions, caregivers of elderly
workaround: fridge sheets, phone medical ID, wallet cards

title: Wandering and getting lost
problem: A relative with dementia leaves the house unnoticed or gets disoriented on a familiar walk, and the family has no way to locate them quickly.
workaround: door alarms, GPS trackers in shoes, ID bracelets

title: Daily check-ins on a parent living alone
problem: A caregiver worries every morning whether their elderly parent is up and okay, and a missed phone call triggers a panic or a drive over.
who: adult children of elderly parents living alone
workaround: scheduled calls, neighbors, smart speakers, motion sensors

title: Dementia patient asking the same question
problem: A parent with dementia asks what day it is or when the appointment is thirty times a day, and the caregiver's patience wears thin answering.
workaround: whiteboards, large-print calendars, dementia clocks

title: Fall detection and help when alone
problem: A person with mobility issues or seizures fears falling when no one is around and being unable to reach a phone to call for help.
who: elderly living alone, people with epilepsy, POTS, MS
workaround: pendant alarms, keeping the phone on a lanyard

title: Medical supplies running out at home
problem: Catheters, ostomy bags, test strips, syringes and dressings run low without warning, and reordering through the durable-supply company takes days.
who: patients using ongoing medical supplies, home carers
workaround: eyeballing the box, keeping a backup stash

title: Home exercise and physio adherence
problem: The physiotherapist hands over a sheet of exercises and the patient forgets the sets, does them wrong, or stops after a week with no feedback loop.
who: patients in physio, cardiac or pulmonary rehab
workaround: paper printouts, YouTube videos

title: Reading nutrition info for a restricted diet
problem: A renal, celiac or low-FODMAP diet means checking every label for potassium, gluten or specific sugars, which makes grocery shopping and eating out slow and stressful.
who: patients on medically restricted diets and their caregivers
workaround: memorized lists, printed guides, avoiding restaurants

title: Doctor dismissing symptoms without documentation
problem: Patients, particularly women and people with chronic pain, feel dismissed when they cannot show a clear record of how often and how badly symptoms occur.
who: people with chronic pain, endometriosis, autoimmune conditions
workaround: bringing a companion, switching doctors, printed logs

title: Explaining an invisible illness to others
problem: Friends, employers and even family repeatedly ask why you cancelled again or 'still' feel sick, and the patient exhausts themselves re-explaining a condition that does not show.
who: people with fibromyalgia, lupus, long COVID, mental illness
workaround: canned messages, withdrawing socially

title: Finding others with the same rare condition
problem: A newly diagnosed rare-disease patient finds no one nearby who understands, and online groups are scattered across Facebook, Reddit and forums of varying quality.
who: people with rare or uncommon diagnoses
workaround: Facebook groups, subreddits, patient advocacy orgs

title: Health anxiety spirals from searching symptoms
problem: Between appointments the patient searches every new sensation and lands on worst-case diagnoses, which fuels anxiety and sometimes makes symptoms worse.
who: patients with chronic conditions and health anxiety
workaround: trying not to google, asking online communities

title: Prior authorization delays and denials
problem: A medication or scan is prescribed, then insurance requires prior authorization, and the patient waits weeks not knowing whether it was submitted, pending or denied.
who: patients on specialty drugs, needing imaging or procedures
workaround: calling insurer and doctor's office repeatedly

title: Copay card and patient-assistance renewals
problem: Manufacturer copay cards and assistance programs expire yearly or run out of funds mid-year, and the patient discovers it at the counter when the price jumps.
who: patients on specialty and biologic drugs
workaround: calendar reminders, re-enrolling after the surprise

title: Drug price varies wildly by pharmacy
problem: The same prescription costs $180 at one pharmacy and $25 with a coupon at another, and the patient only finds out by accident.
workaround: GoodRx-style coupon sites, asking the pharmacist for cash price

title: Understanding medical bills and EOBs
problem: A single hospital visit produces multiple bills from the facility, physician group, lab and anesthesiologist, plus insurer EOBs that do not match, and it is unclear what is actually owed.
workaround: spreadsheets, calling billing departments, paying whatever comes

title: FSA/HSA receipts and eligibility
problem: Receipts for eligible medical expenses are scattered across email and paper, and by year-end the patient has no idea what was already reimbursed or what still qualifies.
who: people with FSA or HSA accounts
workaround: a shoebox of receipts, photos in camera roll

title: Tracking deductible and out-of-pocket progress
problem: Patients cannot tell how close they are to the deductible or out-of-pocket max, so they cannot plan whether to schedule a procedure this year or next.
workaround: insurer portal that lags weeks behind, spreadsheets

title: Checking interactions across prescribers
problem: The cardiologist and the psychiatrist each prescribe without knowing what the other added, and nobody reviews the full list for interactions until a pharmacist happens to flag it.
who: patients with multiple specialists, elderly on many meds
workaround: asking the pharmacist, googling each pair

title: Controlled-substance refill timing window
problem: ADHD stimulants and pain meds can only be refilled within a narrow window and require a fresh prescription each time, so missing the day means going without.
workaround: marking the earliest fill date on a calendar and calling the office in advance

title: Forgetting whether a pill was taken
problem: Twenty minutes after the usual dose time you cannot remember if you actually swallowed the pill or just thought about it, and double-dosing or skipping both have consequences.
who: people on daily maintenance meds, especially memory-affecting conditions
workaround: weekly pill organizers, checking the blister pack, guessing

title: Pharmacy has the drug out of stock
problem: You arrive to pick up a prescription and the pharmacy is out of that medication; you then call pharmacy after pharmacy to find one that has it in stock.
who: patients on drugs in shortage (stimulants, GLP-1s, some antibiotics)
workaround: calling around, asking the pharmacist to check nearby stores

title: Refill request stuck between doctor and pharmacy
problem: The pharmacy says it faxed the doctor, the doctor's office says nothing arrived, and the patient is the one making phone calls while the bottle is empty.
who: patients whose prescriptions need periodic renewal
workaround: calling both sides repeatedly, asking for an emergency 3-day supply

title: Tapering and titration schedules
problem: Doctors write 'take 2 tablets for 5 days, then 1.5 for 5 days, then 1...' and the patient has to compute today's dose every morning and remember where they are in the taper.
who: patients tapering steroids, antidepressants, benzodiazepines, or titrating new meds
workaround: paper chart on the fridge, counting days from the start date

title: Keeping an up-to-date medication list
problem: Every new doctor asks for a full list of current medications and doses, and the patient recites from memory or brings a bag of bottles, often missing recent changes.
who: patients seeing multiple specialists, caregivers of elderly parents
workaround: a folded paper list in the wallet, photos of bottles

title: Refills running out on different days
problem: Each of six prescriptions comes due on a different date, so there is a pharmacy trip almost every week and something is always about to run out.
workaround: asking the pharmacy to sync refills, calendar reminders, keeping a spare bottle

title: Timing meds around food and each other
problem: One pill must be taken on an empty stomach, another with food, a third two hours away from calcium, and the schedule falls apart on any non-routine day.
who: patients with complex regimens (thyroid, osteoporosis, HIV, transplant)
workaround: handwritten schedules, phone alarms for each pill

title: Travelling with medication supplies
problem: Before a trip you have to count out enough of each pill, figure out time-zone dose shifts, and make sure refrigerated drugs like insulin stay cold.
workaround: counting into baggies, cooler packs, guessing at time-zone timing

title: Not knowing what a pill is
problem: A loose tablet is found in a pill organizer or on the floor and no one can tell which medication it is from the imprint and color.
who: caregivers filling organizers, patients with many similar pills
workaround: searching pill identifier websites, calling the pharmacist

title: Disability paperwork and work accommodations
problem: Applying for disability benefits or accommodations means gathering years of records, doctor letters and forms with deadlines, all while too sick to manage it.
workaround: advocates, lawyers, family members doing the paperwork

title: Imaging and records transfer between providers
problem: Getting an MRI or old records to a new specialist means faxes, mailed CDs, or driving a disc across town, and often the images do not arrive in time for the visit.
workaround: requesting CDs and carrying them, signing release forms repeatedly

title: One patient portal per health system
problem: Each hospital and clinic has its own portal login, so lab results, messages and visit notes are scattered across five apps with five passwords.
who: patients seen at multiple health systems
workaround: password manager, screenshots, printing everything

title: Results released before the doctor explains
problem: Portals push raw lab and imaging results to the patient instantly, often on a Friday night, with alarming flagged values and no explanation until the appointment days later.
workaround: googling the terms, anxious waiting

title: Tracking the story of a long diagnosis
problem: Over years of an undiagnosed condition the patient loses track of which tests were done, what was ruled out and which doctor said what.
who: people with rare or hard-to-diagnose conditions
workaround: binders of printouts, long Word documents

title: Lab results without trends or context
problem: Results arrive as a single number with a reference range, with no easy way to see whether it has been climbing for two years or what the previous values were.
who: patients monitoring chronic markers (A1c, creatinine, TSH, cholesterol)
workaround: manually charting in a spreadsheet

title: Re-telling the medical history every time
problem: Every new provider intake asks for the same surgeries, diagnoses, family history and dates, and the patient rewrites it on a clipboard from memory each time.
who: patients with long histories, caregivers filling forms for a parent
workaround: a typed summary carried in a folder

title: Explaining symptoms from memory at appointments
problem: The doctor asks how often the migraines came and how bad they were over the last three months, and the patient can only say 'a lot, some were bad'.
who: people with migraines, IBS, pain conditions, autoimmune flares
workaround: notes app, paper diaries that get abandoned after two weeks

title: Identifying flare triggers
problem: Symptoms flare unpredictably and the patient suspects food, sleep, stress or weather but cannot correlate them without months of consistent data.
who: people with migraine, IBS, eczema, Crohn's, fibromyalgia
workaround: elimination diets, gut feeling, spreadsheets

title: Insulin dosing math at every meal
problem: Counting carbs, applying a ratio, adjusting for current glucose and remaining active insulin has to be done before every meal, and mistakes cause highs or dangerous lows.
who: people with type 1 diabetes and parents of diabetic children
workaround: pump bolus calculators, mental arithmetic, carb-counting books

title: Pacing energy to avoid crashes
problem: Overdoing it on a good day causes a multi-day crash, but there is no easy way to see how much activity is 'too much' before it is too late.
who: people with ME/CFS, long COVID, POTS, MS
workaround: spoon theory budgeting in the head, heart-rate monitors

title: Bowel and bladder diaries on paper
problem: Specialists ask for a two-week diary of bathroom frequency and characteristics, which is awkward and easily forgotten on paper.
who: IBD, IBS, urology and pelvic-floor patients
workaround: paper sheets from the clinic, notes app

title: Fluid and sodium intake tracking
problem: Patients told to limit fluids or salt, or to hit a daily water target, lose count by mid-afternoon and have no idea whether they are over or under.
who: kidney, heart failure, POTS and dialysis patients
workaround: measuring jugs, tally marks

title: Logging vitals across several devices
problem: Blood pressure, glucose, weight and oxygen readings each live in a different device or app, and the doctor wants them together on one sheet.
who: patients with hypertension, diabetes, heart failure
workaround: handwriting readings in a notebook, photographing the device screen

title: Remembering side effects of a new drug
problem: A new medication is started and weeks later the patient cannot recall when the dizziness began or whether it started before or after the dose increase.
workaround: none, or scattered notes

title: Tracking too tiring on bad days
problem: The days when a symptom log matters most are the days the patient is too exhausted or in too much pain to fill out a detailed form, so the data has gaps exactly where it counts.
who: people with ME/CFS, long COVID, chronic pain, depression
workaround: backfilling from memory, giving up on tracking

title: Task initiation paralysis on simple chores
problem: Knowing exactly what needs doing but being unable to start, even a two-minute task, and feeling shame that grows the longer it sits.
who: adults with ADHD, autistic adults, people with depression
workaround: Body doubling over video, bargaining with oneself, waiting for a deadline panic

title: Breaking big tasks into steps
problem: A project like 'sort out taxes' has no obvious first step, so it stays on the list for months while the deadline creeps closer.
who: adults with ADHD and executive-function difficulties
workaround: Asking a friend to talk it through, AI chat prompts

title: Controlled-substance refill timing chaos
problem: Stimulant prescriptions cannot be refilled early, pharmacies are frequently out of stock, and tracking the earliest refill date and which pharmacy has supply becomes a monthly scramble.
who: adults and parents managing ADHD medication
workaround: Calling pharmacies one by one, calendar notes, Reddit shortage threads

title: Emotional dysregulation after minor setbacks
problem: A small piece of criticism or a perceived rejection triggers an outsized emotional crash that wipes out the rest of the day's plans.
workaround: Therapy skills, venting to friends, avoidance

title: Forgetting whether medication was taken
problem: Twenty minutes after your morning routine you cannot remember whether you took your stimulant, and doubling up or skipping both have real consequences.
who: people on daily ADHD or psychiatric medication
workaround: Pill organizers, photographing the bottle, counting remaining pills

title: Reminders that get dismissed and forgotten
problem: A phone reminder fires while you are mid-task, you swipe it away intending to act later, and it is gone from your mind within seconds.
workaround: Setting five duplicate alarms or leaving the reminder unread on purpose

title: Time blindness before appointments
problem: You cannot feel how much time is left before you need to leave, so you are either 40 minutes early or 20 minutes late, with nothing in between.
workaround: Multiple countdown alarms, visual timers, asking a partner to nudge

title: Transition between tasks feels impossible
problem: Stopping one activity to begin another, even a pleasant one, produces disproportionate resistance and the change gets delayed for hours.
who: autistic adults and people with ADHD
workaround: Advance warnings, rigid schedules, timers with escalating alerts

title: Abandoned to-do apps graveyard
problem: Every task app works for two weeks, then the novelty fades, the list becomes a wall of overdue red, and opening it feels like being scolded.
workaround: Switching apps, paper lists, sticky notes on the monitor

title: Doom piles and doom boxes
problem: Miscellaneous items get dumped in a pile or box 'to deal with later', and the pile grows until sorting it becomes overwhelming.
workaround: Periodic purges, moving the box to another room

title: Finding a body double on demand
problem: Working alongside another person helps you focus, but there is nobody available right when you need to start, and scheduling a session is itself a task.
who: remote workers and students with ADHD
workaround: Discord study rooms, Focusmate, calling a friend

title: Hyperfocus erases meals and breaks
problem: You look up from a task and six hours have passed without eating, drinking, or moving, and you now feel awful.
who: people with ADHD and autistic adults
workaround: Interval alarms that get ignored

title: Out of sight, out of mind items
problem: Anything put in a drawer, cupboard or folder effectively ceases to exist, leading to duplicate purchases, expired food and missed paperwork.
workaround: Clear bins, leaving everything on surfaces, labeling

title: Reading long emails and losing the ask
problem: A dense email or Slack thread contains one actual request buried in paragraphs, and you skim, miss it, and get chased later.
workaround: Asking the sender to bullet it, re-reading three times

title: Going nonverbal with no quick way to communicate
problem: During shutdown or overload speech becomes unavailable, and there is no fast way to tell people around you what is happening or what you need.
workaround: Pre-written cards, typing in Notes and showing the screen

title: Masking exhaustion goes untracked
problem: After a day of performing neurotypical behavior you crash, but the link between specific social loads and the burnout is invisible until it is too late.
workaround: Energy accounting ('spoons'), cancelling plans reactively

title: Phone calls required for basic services
problem: Doctors, landlords and utilities insist on phone calls, and the unpredictability of live conversation causes hours of dread and postponed tasks.
who: autistic adults, people with anxiety, deaf and hard-of-hearing people
workaround: Scripting the call, asking a family member to call, avoiding the task

title: Safe foods running out
problem: A narrow set of tolerated foods means a discontinued product, recipe change or empty shelf can leave nothing acceptable to eat.
who: autistic people and those with ARFID
workaround: Stockpiling, checking multiple stores, eating nothing

title: Sensory overload in shops and transit
problem: Fluorescent lights, background music, crowds and announcements stack up until you have to leave a supermarket mid-shop or miss your stop.
who: autistic adults, people with sensory processing differences
workaround: Noise-cancelling headphones, sunglasses, shopping at odd hours

title: Unexpected plan changes derail the day
problem: A cancelled appointment or a friend arriving late throws off a carefully structured day and the fallout can last hours.
workaround: Backup plans, over-communicating, avoiding plans with unreliable people

title: Unknown sensory environment of new venues
problem: Before visiting a restaurant, clinic or venue you cannot find out how loud, bright or crowded it is, so you either avoid it or risk a meltdown.
who: autistic people and parents of autistic children
workaround: Phoning ahead, checking photos, arriving at opening time

title: Decoding tone in text messages
problem: A short reply like 'ok.' or 'fine' can be read as anger or dismissal, leading to hours of rumination about whether someone is upset.
who: autistic adults, people with rejection sensitivity
workaround: Asking directly, screenshotting to friends for a second opinion, tone indicators

title: Interoception blind spots
problem: Not noticing hunger, thirst, tiredness or needing the toilet until it becomes urgent or turns into a headache and irritability.
workaround: Scheduled eating and drinking, tracking apps

title: Unwritten social scripts for common situations
problem: Interactions like checking into a hotel, small talk with a barber or declining an invitation have unstated expectations that must be worked out from scratch each time.
workaround: Memorized scripts, rehearsing, watching how others do it

title: Visual schedules that don't update
problem: Printed picture schedules for a child fall out of date the moment plans change, and remaking them with laminated cards is slow.
who: parents and teachers of autistic children
workaround: Velcro card boards, whiteboards, printing new cards

title: Touchscreen appliances and kiosks
problem: Flat touchscreen microwaves, washing machines, self-checkouts and ticket kiosks give no tactile or audio feedback, so they cannot be operated independently.
workaround: Tactile bump stickers, memorizing button sequences, asking staff

title: Unlabeled buttons in apps
problem: Screen readers announce 'button, button, button' because icons have no labels, making core features of mainstream apps unusable.
workaround: Guessing by position, asking sighted help, emailing developers

title: Finding the entrance and the right door
problem: GPS gets you to the address but not to the actual door, and once inside there is no way to find the reception desk, the right room or the toilet.
who: blind and low-vision people navigating alone
workaround: Asking passers-by, remote sighted assistance apps, arriving early

title: Identifying cans and packages in the kitchen
problem: Cans, boxes and jars feel identical, and printed labels and cooking instructions are unreadable without sighted assistance.
who: blind and low-vision people cooking at home
workaround: Braille or rubber-band labeling systems, barcode scanning apps, memorizing shelf positions

title: Inaccessible CAPTCHAs block sign-ups
problem: Image-based CAPTCHAs have no working audio alternative or the audio is unintelligible, so you cannot create accounts or log in.
who: blind users and people with cognitive disabilities
workaround: Asking sighted help, browser extensions, abandoning the site

title: Low-contrast text and thin fonts
problem: Light grey text on white and hairline fonts are unreadable even with zoom, and zooming breaks layouts so buttons disappear off screen.
workaround: High-contrast modes, browser zoom, reader view, custom CSS

title: Which bus is this at the stop
problem: Several buses arrive at once and there is no audio announcement of the route number, so you may board the wrong one or miss yours.
workaround: Asking the driver, asking others at the stop, live vehicle tracking apps

title: Images and memes with no alt text
problem: Friends share screenshots and memes in group chats and social feeds that arrive as silent 'image' to a screen reader, leaving you out of the conversation.
who: blind and low-vision social media users
workaround: Asking what the picture is, AI image description tools

title: Reading mail and bills that arrive on paper
problem: Letters, bills and official notices come in print and must be photographed and OCR'd one page at a time, or wait for a sighted person.
workaround: Phone camera OCR apps, family reading it, requesting large print or email

title: Matching clothes and checking for stains
problem: Choosing an outfit that matches and is clean requires colour and stain information that is not available by touch.
workaround: Colour identifier apps, buying only neutral colours, labeling hangers

title: Coordinating a child's therapy schedule
problem: Speech, occupational and behavioral therapy sessions, school meetings and specialist appointments overlap and change, with paperwork from each provider.
who: parents of autistic or disabled children
workaround: Shared calendars, binders, spreadsheets

title: Requesting accommodations is unclear
problem: Working out what you are entitled to at work or university, how to word the request and what documentation is needed takes weeks of research and emails.
who: neurodivergent and disabled students and employees
workaround: Advocacy groups, templates from forums, asking others who have done it

title: Autoplay and flashing content triggers
problem: Autoplaying videos, animated ads and flashing effects cause distraction, migraines or seizures, and per-site settings do not persist.
who: people with ADHD, photosensitive epilepsy, vestibular disorders
workaround: Browser extensions, reduced-motion settings, avoiding sites

title: Explaining a condition to every new person
problem: Each new doctor, teacher or manager needs the same explanation of how your condition affects you and what helps, and it is exhausting to repeat.
who: neurodivergent and disabled people, parents of disabled children
workaround: Prepared 'about me' documents, hospital passports, memorized speech

title: Keeping routines during travel
problem: Hotels, time zones and unfamiliar shops break carefully built medication, meal and sleep routines, and the disruption takes days to recover from.
who: autistic people, people with ADHD, people on strict medication schedules
workaround: Packing lists, bringing safe foods, extra alarms

title: Screen-reader friendliness of a site unknown
problem: Before spending time on a new shop or service you cannot tell whether checkout will work with assistive tech, and you often find out at the last step.
workaround: Community recommendations, trial and error, sticking to known sites

title: Waiting-room and queue uncertainty
problem: Sitting in an unpredictable waiting room with no idea how long it will be is distressing, and stepping out to regulate risks losing your place.
who: autistic people, people with anxiety, people with ADHD
workaround: Asking reception repeatedly, waiting in the car, headphones

title: Businesses that only take phone bookings
problem: Clinics, restaurants and tradespeople with no online booking or text option are effectively closed to you, or require a relay service that many hang up on.
workaround: Relay services, asking a hearing friend, choosing only businesses with online booking

title: Group conversations in noisy restaurants
problem: Following several people talking over background noise is impossible, so you nod along and miss the plans being made.
who: deaf and hard-of-hearing people, people with auditory processing disorder
workaround: Live transcription apps, sitting with your back to the wall, leaving early

title: Missing doorbells, alarms and announcements
