problem: Deliveries are missed because the doorbell is not heard, and airport or train platform changes are announced only by loudspeaker.
workaround: Flashing-light doorbells, watching departure boards constantly, asking staff

title: Video calls with fast-talking colleagues
problem: Meeting captions lag, speakers talk over each other, and lipreading fails when cameras are off, so you leave meetings unsure what was decided.
workaround: Asking for written summaries, recording and re-watching, live captioners

title: Videos and live streams without captions
problem: Social media videos, online courses and workplace recordings often have no captions or auto-captions so wrong they are useless.
workaround: Requesting transcripts, third-party captioning tools, skipping the content

title: Drive-throughs and intercoms
problem: Ordering at drive-throughs, buzzing into apartment buildings and speaking to parking-garage intercoms all depend on hearing a crackly speaker.
workaround: Going inside, pre-written cards, mobile ordering apps

title: Hearing-aid battery and connectivity failures
problem: Rechargeable hearing aids die mid-day, Bluetooth pairing drops, and there is no warning until conversation suddenly vanishes.
workaround: Carrying spare batteries, restarting the phone, manufacturer apps

title: Mixing up similar-looking numbers
problem: Transposing digits in phone numbers, bank details or dates leads to failed payments and missed appointments, and the error is hard to spot on review.
workaround: Copy-paste only, reading numbers aloud, asking someone to double check

title: Reading aloud in meetings or class
problem: Being asked to read a passage aloud on the spot causes panic and stumbling, and there is no discreet way to preview or get support.
workaround: Pre-reading, declining, disclosing the disability

title: Reading on screens with dense text
problem: Long paragraphs in small fonts on white backgrounds cause letters to swim and lines to be re-read, so articles and documentation take three times longer.
who: people with dyslexia and visual stress
workaround: Browser reader mode, overlays, text-to-speech, giving up

title: Scanned PDFs that can't be read aloud
problem: Work and school documents arrive as image-only PDFs that text-to-speech tools cannot read, so the content is locked away.
who: students and workers with dyslexia, blind and low-vision users
workaround: Running OCR manually, asking for an accessible version, skipping the reading

title: Paper forms at clinics and offices
problem: Handwritten forms in waiting rooms must be filled in under time pressure with no spellcheck or dictation, causing embarrassment and errors.
who: people with dyslexia or dysgraphia, people with tremor
workaround: Bringing a companion, asking for the form in advance, leaving fields blank

title: Spellcheck can't guess dyslexic spellings
problem: When a word is spelled phonetically or with letters transposed, standard spellcheck offers no useful suggestion, and searching for the word also fails.
workaround: Voice dictation, asking someone, describing the word to a search engine

title: Booking wheelchair-accessible taxis
problem: Ride-hailing apps rarely have accessible vehicles available, wait times are far longer, and drivers sometimes cancel on seeing a wheelchair.
workaround: Booking hours ahead, local taxi firms, paratransit schemes

title: Step-free route unknown before travel
problem: Map apps route you via stairs, broken lifts and kerbs without dropped curbs, and you only discover it when you are stuck in front of them.
who: wheelchair users, people with mobility impairments, parents with prams
workaround: Street View scouting, phoning venues, transit lift-status pages

title: Accessible toilet location and access
problem: Finding an accessible toilet nearby, knowing whether it is locked, needs a key, or is being used as storage, is a constant unknown when out.
who: wheelchair users and people with continence conditions
workaround: Radar key schemes, crowd-sourced toilet maps, limiting fluid intake

title: Blocked accessible parking and ramps
problem: Disabled bays are taken by non-permit cars and ramps are blocked by bins or delivery vans, and reporting it is slow or pointless.
workaround: Driving around, confronting drivers, reporting to the council

title: Energy budgeting on bad pain days
problem: Not knowing how much energy tomorrow will hold means over-committing and then cancelling everything, or under-committing and losing days.
who: people with chronic pain, fatigue or mobility conditions
workaround: Spoon theory tracking, pacing diaries, keeping days empty

title: Tiny touch targets and precise gestures
problem: Small buttons, swipe-to-delete gestures and drag-and-drop are error-prone with tremor or limited dexterity, leading to accidental taps and sends.
who: people with tremor, arthritis, cerebral palsy or motor impairments
workaround: Styluses, accessibility touch settings, voice control, asking someone

title: Venue 'accessible' claims that are wrong
problem: Restaurants and hotels say they are accessible, but there is a step at the door, the lift is tiny or the accessible room has a bathtub.
who: wheelchair users and people with limited mobility
workaround: Calling to ask specific questions, asking for photos, relying on word of mouth

title: Voice control fails in web forms
problem: Dictation and voice navigation work in some fields but not others, so a form has to be abandoned halfway or completed by someone else.
who: people with limited hand use who rely on voice input
workaround: Switching devices, browser extensions, asking for assistance

title: Finding a consistent D&D session time
problem: The most common reason campaigns die is that four to six adults cannot find a recurring slot, and every session requires renegotiation.
workaround: When2meet, Discord polls, giving up

title: Running a tabletop RPG campaign's notes
problem: Game masters juggle NPC names, plot threads, maps and player backstories across notebooks and Google Docs, and players forget what happened last session.
who: Dungeons & Dragons and other TTRPG groups
workaround: Obsidian vaults, World Anvil, binders

title: Board game night scheduling and headcount
problem: Game night depends on knowing exactly how many people are coming, because most games have hard player counts, and last-minute drops leave a five-player game with three.
workaround: Group chats, Doodle, guessing

title: Missing pieces discovered mid-game
problem: A game is set up before anyone realizes a card or token is missing, and finding the publisher's replacement-parts form takes ages.
who: Board game owners, especially secondhand buyers
workaround: Improvising with coins, publisher parts requests

title: Re-teaching rules after months
problem: Nobody remembers the rules of a game played once last year, and reading the rulebook aloud kills thirty minutes of the evening.
workaround: YouTube how-to-play videos, player-aid cards

title: Choosing a game for the group tonight
problem: With a shelf of fifty games, hosts struggle to pick one that fits the player count, time available and the mix of newbies and veterans present.
workaround: BoardGameGeek collection filters, arguing

title: Scorekeeping for complex games
problem: End-game scoring in heavy euros involves many categories and errors are common, and score sheets run out or get lost.
workaround: Paper pads, phone calculators, official companion apps

title: Tracking who won which games over time
problem: Groups want to know play counts, win rates and streaks for bragging rights but have no record of past plays.
workaround: BG Stats app, spreadsheets, memory

title: Building and tracking a deck for card games
problem: Players of Magic, Pokemon or Lorcana lose track of which cards are in which deck and which are loose, so building a new deck means dismantling another.
workaround: Moxfield, Archidekt, deck boxes with labels

title: Buying a duplicate at a shop or show
problem: At a convention, record store or flea market, collectors cannot remember whether they already own a particular issue, pressing or variant and buy it again.
who: Comic, vinyl, trading card and coin collectors
workaround: Photos on phone, want lists on paper, collection apps

title: Cataloguing a large collection takes forever
problem: Entering hundreds of items one by one into a database is so tedious that most collectors never finish, leaving them with no record for insurance.
workaround: Barcode-scanning apps, spreadsheets, giving up

title: Not knowing a collection's total value
problem: Collectors of cards, coins, vinyl or figures have no idea what their collection is worth for insurance or sale, and prices shift constantly.
workaround: Spreadsheets with manual price lookups, Discogs, TCGplayer

title: Remembering paint recipes for miniatures
problem: Painters cannot reproduce a color scheme on the next batch of miniatures months later because the layered paint recipe was never written down.
workaround: Notebooks, photos, paint-recipe apps

title: Storing and finding physical items later
problem: Collectors know they own an item but cannot find which box, binder or shelf it is in without emptying the closet.
who: Collectors who store items in bins and binders
workaround: Labels, memory, photos of box contents

title: Tracking a want list across marketplaces
problem: The specific card or figure a collector needs shows up on eBay, Mercari or a forum at a good price and is gone before they see it.
workaround: eBay saved searches, checking multiple sites daily

title: Tracking model kit and miniature backlog
problem: Miniature painters and model builders accumulate a 'pile of shame' of unbuilt kits and forget which paints they need for which project.
who: Warhammer painters, Gundam and scale model builders
workaround: Spreadsheets, photos, guilt

title: Forgetting paint colors and finishes used
problem: Touching up a wall years later fails because nobody remembers the exact paint brand, color code and sheen, and the leftover can has dried out.
workaround: Writing on the can, photos of the lid, guessing at the store

title: Half-finished DIY projects around the house
problem: A weekend project stalls for months because the next step needs one part or one dry day, and by then the plan and measurements are forgotten.
who: Homeowners doing their own repairs and builds
workaround: Notes app, nagging from partner

title: Multiple trips to the hardware store
problem: DIYers go to the store three times per project because the cut list or fastener count was estimated from memory and something was missed.
workaround: Handwritten lists, buying extra of everything

title: Optimizing board cuts to reduce waste
problem: Figuring out how to cut a plywood sheet or lumber into needed pieces with minimal offcuts is error-prone on paper, and mistakes waste expensive material.
workaround: Graph paper, online cut optimizers

title: Tracking 3D printer filament and settings
problem: 3D printing hobbyists forget which filament spool has how much left and which temperature settings worked for it, leading to failed prints and mid-print run-outs.
workaround: Spreadsheets, weighing spools, notes on the spool

title: Saving project inspiration that is findable later
problem: Ideas from Pinterest, YouTube and Instagram get saved in five places, and when it is time to build the bookshelf nobody can find the video with the joinery detail.
workaround: Pinterest boards, browser bookmarks, screenshots

title: Tool inventory and lending loss
problem: Tools lent to neighbors or friends never come back, and owners cannot remember who has the drill or the ladder.
workaround: Memory, asking around

title: Losing your place in a knitting pattern
problem: Knitters and crocheters lose count of rows and repeats when interrupted, then have to rip back hours of work after discovering the mistake.
workaround: Row counters, tally marks, sticky notes on the pattern

title: Calculating fabric or yarn needed for a size
problem: Adjusting a pattern for a different size or gauge requires math many crafters get wrong, leading to running out of material or wasted purchases.
workaround: Calculator and scrap paper, buying extra

title: Craft supply hoard with unknown contents
problem: Beads, paper, paint, fabric scraps and tools fill drawers, and people rebuy items they already own because nothing is catalogued or findable.
workaround: Clear bins, labels, occasional purges

title: Cross-stitch chart tracking on paper
problem: Following a large multi-color chart on paper means highlighting stitched areas by hand and losing the place when the printout gets folded or lost.
workaround: Highlighter pens, Pattern Keeper app, magnet boards

title: Pricing handmade items for sale
problem: Makers who sell at craft fairs or Etsy underprice because they do not track material cost and hours per item and feel awkward charging for labor.
workaround: Rules of thumb, spreadsheets, guessing

title: Too many works in progress abandoned
problem: Half-finished projects pile up in bags, and crafters forget which needles, yarn and pattern belong to which one, so nothing ever gets completed.
workaround: Project bags, Ravelry project pages, guilt

title: Yarn stash nobody can inventory
problem: Crafters forget what yarn they own, in what weight and yardage, and buy duplicates or run short mid-project because they cannot check the stash from the store.
workaround: Ravelry stash pages, spreadsheets, bins with labels

title: Frost warning missed overnight
problem: A surprise late frost kills seedlings because weather apps do not warn at the garden's microclimate level or in time to cover plants.
workaround: Checking forecasts nightly in spring, row covers

title: Missing the sowing window for vegetables
problem: Gardeners realize in June they should have started tomatoes indoors in March, because seed timing depends on local frost dates that packets do not know.
workaround: Almanac charts, seed packet math, spreadsheets

title: Forgetting what was planted where
problem: By midsummer the plant labels have faded or blown away and gardeners cannot tell which tomato variety is which, so they cannot repeat successes next year.
workaround: Paper garden journals, photos, plastic labels

title: Forgetting when to water each plant
problem: Houseplant owners over- or under-water because every plant has different needs and they cannot remember when they last watered which one.
who: Houseplant owners with more than a handful of plants
workaround: Finger test, reminder apps like Planta, watering on a fixed day

title: Glut of harvest with nowhere to go
problem: Zucchini and tomatoes all ripen at once and gardeners cannot use, preserve or give away enough before it rots.
workaround: Leaving bags on neighbors' porches, canning marathons

title: Identifying a pest or disease on a plant
problem: Yellow leaves or spots could be dozens of things, and searching images gives contradictory advice while the plant declines.
workaround: Facebook groups, extension office, guessing

title: Planning crop rotation between seasons
problem: Rotating plant families across beds each year to avoid disease requires remembering last year's layout, which nobody wrote down.
workaround: Graph paper sketches, memory

title: Seed packets expiring unnoticed
problem: Half-used seed packets accumulate for years and gardeners sow old seed that fails to germinate, wasting a season's slot.
workaround: Shoebox sorting, germination tests

title: Finding a local hobby group or club
problem: Newcomers to a hobby or a city cannot easily find the local knitting circle, board game meetup or garden club, and Meetup listings are often dead.
who: People new to a hobby or area
workaround: Facebook groups, library notice boards, asking at shops

title: Hobby spending creeping out of control
problem: Small purchases of yarn, games, plants or supplies add up unnoticed, and people are shocked at the total when they finally look at the bank statement.
workaround: Budgeting apps, self-imposed 'no buy' months

title: Balancing hobby time across several hobbies
problem: People with multiple hobbies feel they neglect all of them, cannot tell how much time each got this month, and lose momentum in the ones they skipped.
who: Adults juggling several hobbies with work and family
workaround: Calendar blocks, habit trackers

title: Documenting progress to see improvement
problem: Hobbyists cannot see how much better their painting, playing or crafting has gotten because early work is not photographed or dated, so they feel stuck.
workaround: Camera roll, Instagram accounts

title: Finding accurate chords or tabs for a song
problem: Tab and chord sites are full of wrong versions, transposed keys, popups and paywalls, so players waste time verifying by ear which version is right.
who: Guitarists, ukulele and piano players learning songs
workaround: Comparing multiple versions on Ultimate Guitar; slowing down YouTube

title: Finding people to jam with nearby
problem: Hobby musicians struggle to find others of similar skill, taste and schedule in their area, and Craigslist-style ads attract flakes.
workaround: Facebook groups, music store bulletin boards, open mics
